In the 2018-19 season, Como were in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football, after going bankrupt twice in the previous 15 years. Last season, the small northern Italian club finished fourth after an extraordinary campaign, producing a series of outstanding performances that surprised the football world.

Sports.title: On the spot: 50 of the most famous – and infamous – Panenka penalties of all time
Sports.content:
It is 50 years since Antonin Panenka won the European Championship for Czechoslovakia with the most audacious penalty ever taken. His signature chip wasn’t instantly eponymous. A search of the British newspaper archives shows that it was barely mentioned until Francesco Totti dusted it off for the internet generation at Euro 2000.

It was at least another decade before Panenka was commonly used as a noun, and it did not have its own Wikipedia page until 2014, but in 2026 every football fan has an idea of what it means. The 50th anniversary is the perfect time to remember 50 of the most famous – and infamous – attempts.

A Panenka is in the eye of the beholder. Ben Lyttleton, doyen of penalties and author of the superb Twelve Yards, asked the man himself what constituted a true Panenka. Their criteria is strict, based on the line of the ball, its trajectory and where it hits the net. But that disqualifies, among others, Zinedine Zidane in the 2006 World Cup final (“This penalty is the obvious misuse of the Panenka classification!”), so we’ve used a looser definition. If the ball was kissed rather than kicked, the penalty is eligible. Rob Smyth

View image in fullscreen The man himself, pictured earlier this year. Photograph: Björn Steinz/The Guardian

Antonin Panenka, 1976

Czechoslovakia 2-2 West Germany (5-3 pens)

This one needs no introduction. RS

Antonin Panenka, 1979

Czechoslovakia 2-0 France

The next high-profile Panenka came almost three years after Belgrade, when he fooled the France keeper Dominique Dropsy with a sensual chip in a vital European Championship qualifier. Czechoslovakia ultimately pipped an emerging France – Michel Platini et al – and finished third at Euro 80. RS

Diego Maradona, 1984

Napoli training

Most of Diego Maradona’s penalties were high-wire acts, Panenkas in spirit, with the ball pointedly passed nowhere near the corner to ensure maximum vaccination. We can’t find any examples of him taking an actual Panenka in a professional game, so we’re including one he took in training at Napoli. Two reasons: one, it’s Maradona; and two, the arc of his penalty shouldn’t be possible. But then we’d already seen him do it in open play. RS

Eric Cantona, 1989

Bordeaux 1-1 Beauvais (3-4 pens)

In February 1989, Eric Cantona was famed more for attitude than ability, having served bans for a tackle of comic-book violence, insulting the France coach, and greeting a friendly substitution by blootering the ball into crowd and tossing his shirt. So Marseille loaned him to Bordeaux and, when a cup game against lower-division Beauvais went to penalties, he went last. Juggling his way to the spot, he tried a Panenka, but the effort held up in the wind before landing in a puddle, allowing the keeper, who’d gone the wrong way, to wander over and pick it up, confirming the upset. Daniel Harris

Gianluca Vialli, 1990

Monaco 2-2 Sampdoria

In the 20th century, certainly in England, a Panenka was generally referred to as a “cheeky chip”. It was also a favourite of a cheeky chap. Gianluca Vialli scored several for Sampdoria, often under extreme pressure: against Genoa in the Scudetto-winning season of 1990-91, and twice during Samp’s Cup Winners’ Cup triumph of 1989-90. The first was against Borussia Dortmund in the last 16, the second in the first leg of the semi-final against Arsène Wenger’s Monaco. Vialli scored two goals in four minutes that night, then two in three when Sampdoria beat Anderlecht 2-0 in the final. RS

Michal Bilek, 1990

Czechoslovakia 5-1 USA

It’s neat that another Czech player was the first to try a Panenka at a World Cup, even if the circumstances were completely different. Czechoslovakia were 4-1 up in a group game against the USA when Michal Bilek, who had already scored one orthodox penalty, tried to pay tribute to 1976. He fluffed it. After making a simple save, the USA keeper Tony Meola barked: “Get that shit outta here!” RS

Gary Lineker, 1992

Nottingham Forest 1-1 Tottenham

Nobody ever talks about the Panenkas that Gary Lineker scored. There were at least three for Tottenham, and we’re pretty sure he’s the first serial Panenka-er in English football. The first completed a hat-trick on live TV – a big deal back in 1990 – and led to a brief post-match discussion in which only one of Elton Welsby and Glenn Hoddle knew about the Euro 76 final. Lineker also scored “a nifty little Panenka”, as he put it, in a Rumbelows Cup semi-final against Nottingham Forest. This one was particularly sweet – the keeper was Mark Crossley, a penalty-saving expert who had denied Lineker from the spot in the previous season’s FA Cup final. RS

Gary Lineker, 1992

England 1-1 Brazil

A kick remembered for comedic reasons, largely through Micah Richards and Alan Shearer chuckling about it every few months on their podcast. But at the time this was a moment of pathos and heartbreak, as Lineker passed up his best, if not his last, chance to equal Bobby Charlton’s all-time England goal record. Jonathan Liew

View image in fullscreen With a share of England’s goalscoring record for the taking, Gary Lineker dinks tamely into the arms of the Brazil goalkeeper Carlos. Illustration: Mark Leech/Offside/Getty Images

Eric Cantona, 1994

Manchester United 1-1 Newcastle United (5-6 pens)

In May 1994, Eric Cantona was untouchable, having inspired Manchester United to a league title then a double. In the FA Cup final, he’d gently rolled two penalties into the same corner of the net, Chelsea’s Dmitri Kharine diving the wrong way as if compelled by the shamanic power of Gallic flair. But in a shootout against Newcastle at that summer’s illustrious Ibrox International Challenge Trophy, the success of his previous Panenka in 1989 persuaded him to try another. Pavel Srnicek obligingly dived out of the way only for the kick to sail over the bar as United lost 6-5. DH

Djalminha, 1995

Guarani 2-1 Internacional

Brazil’s Djalminha, the maverick’s maverick, is best remembered for his signature rainbow flick, so it’s no surprise he was partial to a rainbow kick from the penalty spot. The first of many was scored against Sergio Goycoechea, whose elastic penalty saves had taken Argentina to the final of Italia 90. “I noticed that he always jumped early and committed to a corner,” said Djalminha, “so I thought that was the moment to try the chip.” It quickly became tried and trusted. RS

Dwight Yorke, 1996

Sheffield United 0-1 Aston Villa

Dwight Yorke was so sick of Mark Bosnich saving his penalties in training, he tried something completely different. It worked, so he promised to do it for real the next time Aston Villa were given a spot-kick. That was met with ridicule, but Yorke was true to his word and settled an FA Cup tie at Bramall Lane with a goal that changed his life. “Suddenly,” said Yorke in Born to Score, “the football world was very aware of this cheeky young buck who had dared to execute such an outrageous spot-kick. I definitely detected an increased interest in me after that match.” RS

Gianluca Vialli, 1996

Chelsea 2-4 Wimbledon

There’s no Internet Panenka Database (IPDb), which makes it impossible to say categorically who did what when. But Vialli’s consolation Panenka, at the end of a game in which Chelsea were thrashed by a rampant Wimbledon, may be the first of the Premier League era. Neil Sullivan, who had been beaten from the halfway line by a very different kind of chip earlier in the season, came tantalisingly close to saving it. RS

Dwight Yorke, 1998

Aston Villa 1-0 Arsenal

“If the penalty taker has the bottle to do that, good luck to him,” said David Seaman, who was Panenka-ed on the last day of the 1997-98 season. “There isn’t much a goalie can do except look pretty stupid when it goes in.” Or hold their position, which Seaman did when Yorke took another penalty against him nine months later in an epic league match between Manchester United and Arsenal. His bluff called, Yorke sidefooted wide. RS

John Eyre, 1999

Torquay 0-1 Hull City

If only there was a transcript of the great Neville Southall’s internal monologue as this piece of effrontery floated gently past him. RS

Francesco Totti, 2000

Netherlands 0-0 Italy (1-3 pens)

In their Euro 2000 semi-final with the co-hosts, Italy put on a defensive masterclass while down to 10 men. In the inevitable shootout, Frank de Boer was denied by Francesco Toldo and Jaap Stam blasted his kick into orbit. Stam was immediately followed by Francesco Totti, whose falling leaf penalty foxed Edwin van der Sar and had the Dutch lurching towards despair. It also introduced the Panenka to a new generation. John Brewin

View image in fullscreen Francesco Totti brings the Panenka into the 21st century. Illustration: Henri Szwarc/Bongarts/Getty Images

Mixu Paatelainen, 2001

Hibernian 0-0 Hearts

A last-minute penalty to win an Edinburgh derby is the stuff of dreams – and nightmares. Mixu Paatelainen only took it because Hibs’ usual taker, Russell Latapy, had gone awol two days earlier. After scoring a hat-trick against Hearts earlier in the season, Paatelainen probably thought he could do anything. As his chipped effort sailed over the bar, he was disabused of the notion. RS

Thierry Henry, 2003

Arsenal 3-2 Newcastle

Five days after the Battle of Old Trafford, Arsenal kickstarted their Invincible season with a ding-dong win over Bobby Robson’s Newcastle. The winner was teased softly down the middle by Henry. Maybe it was an unspoken message of defiance that Arsenal would continue to do things their own way. Maybe it meant nothing. Or maybe he was just trolling Ruud van Nistelrooy. RS

View image in fullscreen Thierry Henry went full va-va-voom for his winning penalty against Newcastle. Illustration: Jamie McDonald/Getty Images

Mickaël Landreau, 2004

Nantes 1-1 Sochaux (4-5 pens)

For all the spot-kicks these keepers face, surely they’d understand the right and wrong way to disguise a Panenka. Not poor Mickaël Landreau. He had the chance to secure the 2004 Coupe de la Ligue final for Nantes, but his headlong dash failed to give his lob the requisite power. Sochaux ultimately flipped the result and won the cup. Jeff Rueter

Liam Lawrence, 2004

Huddersfield 0-0 Mansfield (4-1 pens)

Liam Lawrence scored 12 penalties, one short of Francis Lee’s English league record, to help Mansfield to the Third Division playoff final in 2003-04. When that game wheezed to a penalty competition, Lawrence was standing on the halfway line with his teammate Bobby Hassell (“a proper angry little fella”). On the Under the Cosh podcast, Lawrence remembered their exchange.

double quotation mark LL I’m gonna dink it. BH No you’re not. LL I am, honestly. I’m gonna dink it down t’middle. He’s gonna dive; there’s no way he’s gonna stand there in a playoff final. BH Liam, don’t you fuckin’ dink that ball.

He dinked that ball against the bar – “I got too much juice in my run-up” – to leave Mansfield 2-0 down after two penalties. “By the way,” Lawrence added, “the keeper did dive.” RS

Helder Postiga, 2004

Portugal 2-2 England (6-5 pens)

Helder Postiga was a typical Tottenham signing of the era: a talent unfulfilled, sold at a loss after a single Premier League goal. His revenge on English football was to equalise in normal time of the Euro 2004 quarter-final and then send David James stumbling with Portugal’s sixth penalty, a kick so under-amped it barely scraped over the line. Then Darius Vassell missed, the Portugal keeper Ricardo scored, and a tournament that England’s golden generation could have won had slipped from their grasp. JB

Peter Crouch, 2006

England 6-0 Jamaica

The then-Liverpool striker scored an England hat-trick as part of World Cup preparations, yet many only remember him lifting the ball well over the bar from 12 yards. Arrogance certainly played its part, wanting to secure his treble in style, but he had to wait, earning the ire of the usually calm Sven-Göran Eriksson. “It was a golden opportunity to practise for a penalty shootout, but he made a joke out of it,” the head coach spewed. “He’s apologised.” Will Unwin

View image in fullscreen Judging by his expression, Peter Crouch knew he’d got his penalty wrong as soon as he hit it. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images

Artem Milevskiy, 2006

Ukraine 0-0 Switzerland (3-0 pens)

You’re excused if you don’t remember this one: it came after 120 minutes of the most soporific football ever played. RS

Zinedine Zidane, 2006

Italy 1-1 France (5-3 pens)

The nerve to do it in a World Cup final. The scene was nothing new for Zidane. He’d already bagged that brace eight years earlier against Brazil; it had to be him, in his last game, dinking it off the crossbar, past Gianluigi Buffon. It was going to be the dream sendoff – until Marco Materazzi and the anger took over. Taha Hashim

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane steps up… Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

View image in fullscreen … and beats Gianluigi Buffon all ends up. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Archive/PA Images

Yann Kermogant, 2010

Cardiff 2-3 Leicester (agg: 3-3; 4-3 pens)

To miss a Panenka is to embrace infamy. To do so in a Championship playoff is to be consumed by notoriety. In a shootout, with the decisive kick? Insanity. Kermogant, a useful French striker who found his home in England’s second tier, dollied his kick into the body of the grateful Cardiff keeper, David Marshall. Kermogant is remembered for this moment above all others, possibly for eternity. He even has his own Bonnie Tyler adaptation. JB

Sebastián Abreu, 2010

Uruguay 1-1 Ghana (4-2 pens)

If we were picking a Panenka XI, Sebastián Abreu would be one of the first names on the team sheet, so it’s apt that he administered one at a World Cup. A tumultuous quarter-final, best remembered for Luis Suárez’s handball and Asamoah Gyan missing a penalty in the last minute of extra-time, ended with the softest of executions. RS

Andrea Pirlo, 2012

England 0-0 Italy (2-4 pens)

When England somehow prolonged their Euro 2012 quarter-final against Italy to penalties, and with his team leading 2-1 after two goes each, Joe Hart bounced and laughed, seeking to put Andrea Pirlo off … then plunged towards the corner as the ball wafted gently above him and in. “He felt I was too charged not to dive,” Hart reflected on a mood-switching moment. England missed their next two kicks, with two Italian successes finishing them off. “I saw [Hart] making strange movements, so I hit it like that,” Pirlo confirmed afterwards. DH

View image in fullscreen Andrea Pirlo icily dinks his penalty over a fired-up Joe Hart. Illustration: Matthias Schräder/AP

Sergio Ramos, 2012

Spain 0-0 Portugal (4-2 pens)

For such a tactile defender, Sergio Ramos was surprisingly partial to a tender Panenka. His most important came in the Euro 2012 semi-final against Portugal. Bruno Alves missed Portugal’s next kick and Spain went on to demolish Italy in the final. RS

Maicosuel, 2012

Udinese 1-1 Braga (agg: 2-2; 4-5 pens)

The one that cost €20m. Maicosuel had just joined Udinese from Botafogo when his Panenka was saved in a Champions League playoff against Braga. It was the only miss of the shootout. Udinese, coached by Francesco Guidolin, dropped into the Europa League and the big payday went to Braga. “I still can’t get it out of my head,” said Guidolin six years later. “It stalks me.” RS

Graziano Pellè, 2012

SC Heerenveen 2-2 Feyenoord (6-7 pens)

Sudden death, the last 16 of the cup. You’re the seventh-choice penalty-taker, you have to score or it’s over, and you have the chutzpah to try a Pellènka? RS

Rogério Ceni, 2013

São Paulo 0-0 Corinthians (3-4 pens)

No surprise that one of the great goalscoring keepers should beat his opposite number with a Panenka. His reaction after scoring in this Campeonato Paulista semi-final shootout carried a simple message: it’s not personal, it’s strictly business. His São Paulo team lost anyway; Ceni thought he had kept them alive with a save from Alexandre Pato, but he was fractionally off his line. Pato scored the retake emphatically. RS

Alexandre Pato, 2013

Gremio 0-0 Corinthians (3-2 pens)

Five months later, Pato had to score to keep Corinthians in their Copa do Brasil quarter-final against Grêmio. It was an inopportune time to take one of the worst Panenkas ever seen. RS

Alexis Sánchez, 2015

Chile 0-0 Argentina (4-1 pens)

It’s impossible to top the historic significance of the definitive Panenka, but Alexis Sánchez came closer than anyone. His swaggering penalty, which barely left the ground, won Chile their first Copa América – and unlike Czechoslovakia in 1976, they were the hosts. The playful nature of Sánchez’s winning moment only added to the nationwide euphoria. RS

Aaron Ramsey, 2017

Serbia 1-1 Wales

The Wales team of Gareth Bale, Aaron Ramsey and co regularly made history. In a World Cup qualifier in 2017, Ramsey unwittingly did so by scoring a Panenka at the same end of the same ground in Belgrade where it all began. “I didn’t know,” he said, “but that is quite a nice touch.” In more ways than one. RS

View image in fullscreen Aaron Ramsey does a Panenka more completely than most. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Reuters

George Calintaru, 2017

Juventus Bucuresti 1-2 Steaua Bucuresti

A Panenka can seriously damage your health. When George Calintaru fluffed the chance to equalise for newly-promoted Juventus Bucuresti against Steaua with the last kick of the game, his teammates set upon him in frustration. He then punched a table in the dressing room and broke a finger. RS

Fedor Smolov, 2018

Russia 2-2 Croatia (3-4 pens)

Russia’s shock run to the 2018 World Cup quarter-final was soundtracked by raucous support. The crowd in Sochi met the occasion as a shootout with Croatia was all that stood between them and a semi-final. Pedants may contend that Fedor Smolov’s opening attempt lacked enough lob to qualify as a Panenka, but his tame prod up the middle made Danijel Subasic’s job easy to open the sequence in Croatia’s favour. JR

Lionel Messi, 2020

Barcelona 2-2 Atlético Madrid

If you’re going to bring up 700 career goals in an empty stadium, you might as well do it in style. RS

View image in fullscreen Lionel Messi’s penalty record is suprisingly human, but he got the one that gave him his 700th goal right. Photograph: David Ramos/Getty Images

Fara Williams, 2020

Reading 3-1 Aston Villa

This unusual penalty from Fara Williams might not satisfy the Panenka purists. But we’ve included it because it captures a recurring sub-genre: an all-time-great using the Panenka as an expression of undeniable superiority. RS

Ademola Lookman, 2020

West Ham 1-0 Fulham

During his time at Fulham, Ademola Lookman attempted a Panenka against West Ham with the last kick of the game but his feeble chip landed straight in the arms of Lukasz Fabianski. “I’m disappointed and angry,” said his manager Scott Parker in a rare moment of post-match honesty. “You can’t take penalties like that and he knows that.” Yara El-Shaboury

Santi Cazorla, 2021

Al-Gharafa 0-2 Al Sadd

Not many players score orthodox penalties with their left and right feet, never mind Panenkas. Santi Cazorla is a member of the latter club – right foot against Newcastle in 2014, left foot against Al-Gharafa in 2021. RS

Sergio Agüero, 2021

Man City 1-2 Chelsea

City were set to secure the Premier League title but, in front of zero fans during Covid, Sergio Agüero did not feel the pressure. He decided to chip down the middle; Édouard Mendy almost fell for it but had enough time to get up and claim the ball. Chelsea went on to win, and Agüero issued a public apology. WU

View image in fullscreen Sergio Agüero’s Panenka attempt almost, but crucially only almost, fools Édouard Mendy. Photograph: Shaun Botterill/AFP/Getty Images

Marta, 2022

France 2-1 Brazil

Birthday gifts can be a pain to give, especially when the celebrant seems to have given themself the perfect present. Such was life if Marta was on your gift-giving list in 2022, with the Brazilian legend opening that day’s friendly against France in sublime fashion.JR

Karim Benzema, 2022

Manchester City 4-3 Real Madrid

A moment of mischief at the end of a pulsating and painfully serious match. Eight days later, Benzema scored a more orthodox penalty to put Madrid into another Champions League final. RS

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid’s improbable run to winning the 2022 Champions League included Karim Benzema coming up clutch – again. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Achraf Hakimi, 2022

Morocco 0-0 Spain (3-0 pens)

If you’re going to put your country into their first World Cup quarter-final, you might as well do it in style. RS

Gaëtane Thiney, 2023

Real Madrid 0-1 Paris FC

We can’t say for sure that this is the first Panenka in the Women’s Champions League, but it’s definitely the first to knock Real Madrid out of the competition. RS

Antoine Mille, 2024

Les Herbiers 2-2 Châteauroux (3-4 pens)

In which the Les Herbiers goalkeeper Téo Hamelin is so affronted that, after saving one of the more pitiful Panenkas ever taken, he flings the ball straight back at the unfortunate Mille. RS

Marta, 2025

Orlando Pride 2-1 San Diego Wave

If you have already missed your penalty, but opponents’ encroachment has given you a second chance, just how bold do you have to be to attempt a Panenka from the retake? That’s what Marta did in the NWSL for Orlando Pride in 2025, chipping in off the underside of the crossbar to secure a 2-1 victory over San Diego Wave, and remind everybody of her ageless class and skill. Tom Garry

Alexia Putellas, 2025

Roma 0-4 Barcelona

Even the greats fluff their efforts sometimes. Alexia Putellas, one of the best women’s footballers of all time, clipped a Panenka harmlessly over the crossbar during a Champions League victory for Barcelona when her team were only 1-0 up. She redeemed herself from the spot later in the match – that time, tucking safely into the bottom corner. TG

Tiaguinho, 2025

Brazil U17 0-0 Paraguay U17 (5-4 pens)

A Panenka is a dish best served cold. RS

Brahim Díaz, 2026

Morocco 3-0* Senegal

Brahim Díaz had the chance to become a Moroccan hero when he won and then took a stoppage-time penalty that could have ended his country’s 50-year trophy wait. Instead, after a 16-minute delay caused by Senegal’s protests, his Panenka was easily caught by Édouard Mendy. “He had a lot of time before taking the penalty, which must have disturbed him,” said the Morocco manager Walid Regragui. No kidding. Then again … YE-S

View image in fullscreen Brahim Díaz’s miss saw Morocco squander their chance to win the Afcon. Or so we thought… Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images

Mohamed Salah, 2026

Australia 1-1 Egypt (2-4 pens)

Sixty-one penalties were taken at the 2026 World Cup. The surprise is that Mo Salah’s Panenka for Egypt in their shootout against Australia was the only one. Fifty years after it came straight outta leftfield, the Panenka is now firmly part of the mainstream. RS

Sports.title: Football Daily | Scrapped proposals, statement wars and the ongoing Infantino furore
Sports.content:
ANOTHER LONG WEEKEND

Here we go again. And, no, we are not talking about the start of the new Scottish Premiership season or the preliminary round of the Carabao Cup – although that Tranmere v Rochdale shootout was a cracker. Yes, after a week of talk about money, greed and Donald Trump’s son-in-law’s brother, the hot topic around the water cooler on Monday was again Gianni Infantino and, more specifically, the English and Welsh FAs’ decisions to row back on their support of a stalling ship. Along with Finland, they’re the first of Uefa’s 55 members to withdraw their letters of support for next year’s Fifa overlord elections.

By the time Football Daily hits your inboxes, there could be a flurry of other nations frantically clicking unsend on those endorsement emails – more than 200 had their flags planted on Terra Gianni just a matter of weeks ago. This U-turn has us harking back to the hazy days of the €uropean $uper £eague, when the Premier League’s super-elite turned their backs on the super-project one by one. Instead of a handful of club statements and Petr Cech trying to calm protestors on Kings Road, now we could be looking at hundreds of withdrawals from federations across the world. Who will go next? Norway? Japan? Would Gianni pick up the phone to the Oval Office if US Soccer decides enough is enough, maybe to try and get it to reverse the decision? Or at least suspend it until next year.

Either way, the threat of a World Cup boycott is over – for now – after Fifa scrapped its proposal to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors in the early hours of Saturday morning. It was half past midnight in the UK when a statement “attributable to the Fifa president” appeared on its website. That followed a statement called “Clarifications on Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE)” at 4am the night before that doubled down on the plans. It’s not exactly reassuring that such major dealings and decisions are being pondered, seemingly by one man, in the dead of night – but then again, these could be learned behaviours after all.

Statement wars continued with Uefa’s response on Saturday morning, which read: “We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game.” That dubious is doing a lot of work there. Uefa added: “The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa’s confidence, but also that of many other members of the football family.” The first member of the football family out of the traps on Monday morning – once it had given the Cymru Premier’s opening weekend time in the spotlight – was the Welsh FA. It withdrew that precious letter of support for Gianni and proclaimed: “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.” Football Daily waits with bated breath to find out what the next statement will say. The Premier League, after all, is still three weeks away.

RECOMMENDED LOOKING

It’s the 50th anniversary of the first ever Panenka penalty so here is a labour of love/splendid piece of work remembering 50 of the most famous – and infamous – attempts at the Czech’s chip since 1976.

View image in fullscreen The classic. Photograph: Colorsport/Shutterstock

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“Some worried about health problems or being unable to attend because of bad weather, as well as people who frequently travel for work. They are terrified and all asking the same question: will our season tickets be taken away?” – La Provincia, Como’s local paper, says it has received dozens of calls and emails from concerned supporters after the club said it will revoke season tickets from fans who fail to attend four home matches, under a series of new rules.

double quotation mark I write to you with my deep regret on hearing about the death of the heroic and granite-made Franco Baresi. Two moments stand out to me, both off the pitch, and show what a great man he was. The first was when Arrigo Sacchi, the Milan manager, dropped his intensity in training, fearing he was overworking the players; Baresi convinced Sacchi to up it instead for the sake of the team, with spectacular results. The second was an older Baresi reflecting on his 1994 World Cup final loss to Brazil, which he appeared in 25 days after knee surgery. Rather than lamenting his lot, having missed a penalty and lost the final, Baresi instead recalled watching the 1970 final between Italy and Brazil, only the second game he had seen on TV. The first game was the West Germany v Italy semi-final, where he recalled watching the players who ‘to me, they were Martians’. He said: ‘I would never have thought 24 years later, at 34 years old, I would have the possibility to play in that same game, the final, against Brazil, the same team. It was a dream that came true.’ Rest in peace” – Nick Kinsella.

double quotation mark I was wondering if Gianni Infantino might revist his Big Sale Opportunity by allowing smaller, club-level contestants from less lucrative leagues to participate in a seriously revamped World Cup, replacing their boycotting national sides. For instance, from the lower leagues of Scottish competitions. Mainly to render possible the wonderful hypothetical headline result of the last match of the (?) 2038 edition: Fifa Forward Final fiasco … East Fife 4, Forfar 5” – Russell Richardson.

double quotation mark Steve Bennett’s comment on Newcastle United’s new kit (Friday’s Football Daily letters) made me think of West Bromwich Albion’s similarly ‘bar-coded’ Premier League strip from the 2020-21 season, at the end of which they were relegated. Newcastle may have to hope that isn’t an omen” – Derrick Cameron.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Russell Richardson. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea confirmed: England midfielder, 36, joins Blues after ripping up Brentford contract
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed their signing of Jordan Henderson on a free transfer, after Brentford allowed the 36-year-old to terminate his contract a year earlier than expected.

It comes two days after they secured the signature of Danny Welbeck, 35, from Brighton.

Between them, Henderson and Welbeck will add 863 Premier League games’ worth of experience to a changing room now overseen by new manager Xabi Alonso, 44.

Henderson said: 'Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down.

‘I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

‘For me, it's about giving everything every single day, both on and off the field, to help the players around me and the team as much as possible. I'm very excited to get going.’

Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea has been confirmed after he ripped up his Brentford deal

The midfielder was all smiles as he spent the day at Chelsea's Cobham training ground

Henderson, 36, said he was ready to 'give everything every single day, on and off the field'

Alonso identified during his talks to take over Chelsea that their squad was in need of greater balance among the players. The Blues had broken Premier League records for fielding the youngest sides over the previous two seasons, but they had been criticised by fans on occasion for appearing to lack maturity on and off the pitch.

Chelsea previously targeted Granit Xhaka, the 33-year-old Sunderland captain who had worked with Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but were unable to get him out of the Stadium of Light. They likewise showed interest in John Stones, who has now joined Inter Milan at 32.

Yet they have now secured Henderson for free, while the fee for Welbeck is being described as ‘undisclosed’, though his cost is by no means substantial, if indeed there even is one.

Welbeck has already travelled to Hong Kong to join his new team-mates. Daily Mail Sport reported last week how Brentford were ready to sanction Henderson’s exit rather than seek a fee from Chelsea. He is still recovering from the broken arm he suffered with England at the World Cup.

These signings are concrete confirmation that Chelsea have adjusted their transfer strategy by now aiming to add experienced leaders to their squad. Previously, there had been a focus on finding younger players of potential.

Maxence Lacroix, 26 and from Crystal Palace, has already been confirmed by Chelsea for £52million. Morgan Rogers has also arrived for £117m from Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Match delayed by PARROT attack: Incredible moment Brazilian youth game is stopped as bird swoops down on player
Sports.content:
Match delayed by PARROT attack: Incredible moment Brazilian youth game is stopped as bird swoops down on player

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A Brazilian youth game was bizarrely halted at the weekend when a parrot attacked a player.

Flamengo were taking on Ceara in the Brazil Under 15 Cup on Saturday, but the match took an unusual turn just 17 minutes into the first half.

As one Flamengo defender attempted to pass the ball to a team-mate, a blue-and-yellow parrot swooped down towards him, forcing the player to dive to the floor in panic.

The bird then appeared set to go for another player until it flew away at the last moment.

It went on to pester several other players, causing the referee to pause the game, before it eventually flew off.

However, it returned about 25 minutes later when it came down and perched on the pitch, leading to another stoppage.

Parrot ATTACKS soccer player during match between youth teams in Brazil



It definitely bet on the opposing team to win pic.twitter.com/AQ8799Owf3 — RTVisual (@RT_Visual_on_X) August 3, 2026

A Brazilian youth game was bizarrely halted at the weekend when a parrot attacked a player

The parrot went on to pester several other players and caused two stoppages in the match

The bird was later identified as a blue and yellow macaw, a parrot that is typically found in the tropical rainforests of South America.

Flamengo went 1-0 up in the match, but, perhaps impacted by the stoppages, suffered a 2-1 defeat.

The parrot intervention is unusual, but not new, with an amateur game in Turkey between Istanbul Yurdum and Mevlanakapi Guzelhisar halted earlier this year when a seagull was hit by the ball.

The bird dropped to the ground and players rushed to its aid, with the Istanbul captain Gani Catan seen giving CPR to it.

Catan later carried the seagull to the side of the pitch where it received further medical treatment.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes confirms arrival in La Manga as Newcastle REJECT Arsenal bid, Chelsea agree £26m deal to sell Trevoh Chalobah to Como... and Preston skipper is set for controversial £3m exit to Wrexham: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

West Ham in market for Spurs outcast

West Ham are among the clubs interested in signing Manor Solomon from Tottenham.

Solomon has impressed Roberto de Zerbi during a pre season tour of New Zealand and Australia.

De Zerbi knows the Israel international well because they worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk but the winger is set to leave after failing to hold down a place in three years at Spurs.

West Ham are among the clubs interested in signing Manor Solomon from Tottenham

At 27, he is only interested in a permanent move, having spent last season on loan at Villarreal and Fiorentina and the previous season on loan at Leeds, where he sparkled as they won promotion from the Championship to the Premier League.

Fiorentina retain an interest despite not taking up the option on a permanent deal after his loan.

Others are also monitoring the situation, and Spurs have to sell players to clear space in De Zerbi's squad and generate more income.

West Ham are in the market for a winger after selling Crysencio Summerville, but captain Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to the Hammers despite relegation.

Preston boss hits out with Whiteman set for exit to Wrexham

Preston North End have accepted a £3million bid from Wrexham for their wantaway captain Ben Whiteman.

Manager Paul Heckingbottom voiced his displeasure at the weekend, saying Whiteman had crossed a line after telling them he had played his last game for the club in an effort to force through the move.

'Ben knew there was a line I didn't want him to cross and unfortunately he has,' Heckingbottom told BBC Radio Lancashire. 'There's a valuation on him, I just hope for Ben's sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it otherwise he's put himself in a sticky situation. He's made his bed. I'm not bothered as long as I get another player.'

The 30-year-old midfielder is now free to have a medical and complete the transfer, with personal terms not expected to be a problem.

The deal is expected to go through in the next 48 hours and Preston are looking to reinvest the money in another three or four new signings this summer.

Paul Heckingbottom says Ben Whiteman has 'crossed a line' in making his move

Hammers plot £18m bid to land Parrott

West Ham are preparing to outbid European rivals to sign former Tottenham striker Troy Parrott.

The Hammers want to bolster their attack quickly with the new Championship season looming and after being rebuffed for Sunderland's Wilson Isidor, are targeting AZ Alkmaar forward Parrott.

The Republic of Ireland international has interest from Ajax, Como, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis but Alkmaar are reluctant to sell to a Dutch rival.

The Hammers hope an offer of around £18million will be enough to fend off the competition.

Parrott struggled while at Spurs but after an initial loan to Excelsior Rotterdam he began to find his feet and has been prolific with Alkmaar since.

Read more on this story HERE

Troy Parrott celebrates winning the Johan Cruyff Shield with Alkmaar on Sunday

Henderson's relish as he joins Chelsea

Chelsea have announced the signing of 36-year-old Jordan Henderson, after he was allowed to leave Brentford with a year left on his deal.

‘Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down,’ Henderson said.

‘I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

For more on this story click HERE

Jordan Henderson signs on the dotted line as he joins Xabi Alonso's Chelsea revolution

Sunderland block the door to Isidor

West Ham have asked to take Sunderland winger Simon Adingra on loan, but the Wearsiders have no plans to sell forward Wilson Isidor.

West Ham have asked about both players but after initial conversations Sunderland have made it clear that they want to keep Haiti international Isidor.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs over a straight loan for 24-year-old Ivory Coast international Adingra.

Despite interest from a host of clubs, however, Sunderland will not entertain offers for Isidor. The 25-year-old remains an integral part of their squad ahead of their season in European competition and the club believe he can build on an excellent World Cup with Haiti.

West Ham are continuing to discuss AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott while Lazio are interested in the Hammers' German international forward Niclas Fullkrug.

Wilson Isidor is back after the World Cup and Sunderland say he is not for sale despite interest

Como agree £26m Chalobah deal... as Napoli eye Badiashile

Chelsea and Como have agreed a £26million fee for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The deal will include a further £5.2m in add-ons for the 27-year-old England centre-back who is expected to travel to Italy on Wednesday evening.

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile continues to attract interest from Napoli. The Blues are looking to recoup funds for the French centre-back as well as for Axel Disasi who has been the subject of talks with Crystal Palace and West Ham - both are discussing offers.

Disasi had a spell on loan at West Ham last season but ideally wants a top flight offer.

Chelsea hope to make progress with Rayo Vallecano over the purchase of left wing-back Pep Chavarria.

Trevoh Chalobah is on his way to Como, managed by former Blues star Cesc Fabregas

Newcastle reject Arsenal bid for Bruno as he joins Magpies in La Manga

Arsenal's opening bid for Bruno Guimaraes has been rejected by Newcastle. As reported earlier, the clubs are now in direct talks over a deal for Brazilian.

Guimaraes has landed in Spain and is travelling to report back for Newcastle’s pre-season camp in La Manga today.

Newcastle's new manager Matthias Jaissle is at La Manga with the squad and wants to meet the captain.

Bruno Guimaraes is subject of interest from Arsenal but they have not yet made a formal offer

Guimaraes confirmed his arrival in Spain on Instagram on Monday evening

Bernardo gets shirty at Real

Bernardo Silva has arrived at Real Madrid as he joins up with Jose Mourinho's side. The 31-year-old left Manchester City at the end of last season.

The Portugal star, who has returned from the World Cup, was seen signing shirts for fans after medical tests.

🚨 Bernardo Silva continue de signer quelques maillots avant de quitter Sanitas.



🎥 @ainoafrndz pic.twitter.com/7wFAeRQm2F — Le Journal du Real (@lejournaldureal) August 3, 2026

Man United would loan out Chido Obi for game time

Manchester United are willing to send striker Chido Obi Martin out on loan this summer.

The 18-year-old Denmark U21 international had interest from Cologne earlier in the window, but they have moved to sign Jaiden Heskey from Manchester City and are lining up Tottenham winger Mikey Moore.

Chido Obi joined United from Arsenal's academy in 2024 and has made seven first-team appearances though failed to score.

United want to ensure his next club is one where he can develop properly with competitive game time.

Join the queue for Everton's Tim

Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam is attracting increasing interest from rival Premier League clubs and from abroad.

Coventry City, Hull City and Ipswich Town have all made enquiries while two Italian clubs have also asked about the 23-year-old.

Lazio tried to sign the former England U20 international in January.

Everton are continuing to discuss a deal for Arsenal's Christian Norgaard which, if completed, could pave the way for Iroegbunam to depart once a suitable offer comes in.

Everton paid around £9million to Aston Villa for Iroegbunam in 2024.

Tim Iroegbunam joined from Aston Villa two years ago

Coventry keen on Mudryk

Chelsea have received multiple approaches about Mykhailo Mudryk from clubs following the news of his return to football – including three from the Premier League.

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport.

All options are open between Mudryk and Chelsea this summer, including whether to send him out on loan after his sudden comeback from a doping suspension.

Sports.title: World Cup final villain Leandro Paredes sparks another on-pitch melee just weeks after Spain antics - as Argentina thug is booked for classless act
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes was back antagonising opponents on a football pitch at the weekend with some of his antics, but this time at club level.

Paredes' spoiling tactics caught the eye for the wrong reasons last month during Argentina's World Cup semi-final win over England and even more so during his country's abject final defeat by Spain.

He has since returned to club action and played for Boca Juniors in their 2-2 draw at Newell's Old Boys on Sunday in the Argentine Primera Division - Torneo Clausura.

And during that encounter, the 32-year-old was back producing some 'dark arts' with one particular flashpoint.

Trailing 2-1 to the hosts, Paredes started an on-pitch melee when he appeared to deliberately kick a ball at a stricken opponent on 68 minutes.

As the player, who had just been fouled, was returning to his feet and with his back turned, Paredes booted the ball at him.

After controversy at the World Cup, Leandro Paredes has found himself in hot water again 😬 pic.twitter.com/vGSMmG0eRL — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) August 3, 2026

Leandro Paredes sparked a melee during Boca Juniors' 2-2 draw at Newell's Old Boys

Paredes appeared to kick a ball deliberately at a stricken opponent during Sunday's encounter

The 32-year-old's actions saw him booked as he was confronted by Newell's Old Boys players

Paredes threw Spain's Gavi to the floor in disgraceful scenes after the World Cup final in July

The act saw angry players from Newell's Old Boys confront him before the referee brandished him a yellow card for his act.

This latest act follows Paredes' shameful post-match actions after the World Cup final when he bizarrely fought some members of Spain's victorious team.

He grabbed defender Eric Garcia by the neck, pushed over Gavi and also appeared to throw punches after Argentina's defeat. He was also fortunate not to be sent off towards the end of normal time for a foul.

FIFA has since launched disciplinary proceedings against Paredes for the unsavoury scenes - he faces three counts of assault as well as a charge of unsporting behaviour.

Sports.title: England's World Cup nemesis Valentin Barco joins Chelsea: Argentina star who provoked Three Lions in semi-final defeat confirms switch to Stamford Bridge after Atlanta antics
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal.

Barco, 22, who can play in midfield and at left-back, joins the Blues from their sister club Strasbourg.

The Argentine hit the headlines last month when he clashed with Jude Bellingham after England's semi-final defeat at the World Cup.

Barco made just one substitute appearance at the tournament, but he infuriated the Three Lions after he sprinted across the pitch when Enzo Fernandez equalised late on in the clash.

He ran right in front of several England players and appeared to taunt them, before John Stones reacted by giving him a shove.

Barco later also came onto the pitch in the aftermath of Lautaro Martinez's winning goal.

Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal

Barco clashed with Jude Bellingham after Argentina's semi-final victory over England

There were also reports that the new Chelsea star had been winding up the England bench for the entirety of the 90 minutes.

In response to his antics, Bellingham gave the 22-year-old a slap on the back of the head after the full-time whistle as Argentina's players celebrated, causing a scuffle on the pitch.

Given his involvement in the World Cup, Barco won't join up with his new team-mates until later in pre-season.

The versatile star began his career back home with Boca Juniors, making his debut at the age of 16.

After impressing in Argentina, Barco joined Brighton in 2024 for £7.4million yet he struggled to establish himself on the south coast, and spent time on loan at Sevilla and Strasbourg.

He joined Strasbourg permanently in July 2025 and was regularly linked with a move away after impressing in France, where his side qualified for Europe.

Barco contributed 12 goals and assists last season and his strong form saw him earn a place in Argentina's World Cup squad, although he played just 19 minutes in a group stage victory over Jordan.

Bellingham slapped Barco on the back of the head following his overzealous celebrations

His arrival at Stamford Bridge comes following the exit of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid, although Chelsea are still in negotiations with Rayo Vallecano for left wing-back Pep Chavarria after making an improved offer.

Barco is the Blues' seventh signing of the summer, with Danny Welbeck, Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Geovany Quenda, Marco Palestra and former Strasbourg striker Emmanuel Emegha all also joining the club.

He has similarly become the 13th player to move between the French side and Chelsea since BlueCo took over Strasbourg in 2023, a year after they purchased the Premier League side.

Sports.title: Who will win the 2026 Ballon d'Or? Bookies reveal clear favourite as Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi seek prestigious honour - but will one of Spain's World Cup heroes take the prize?
Sports.content:
With the World Cup having concluded, Harry Kane, Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal will be among the stars with their sights set on football's ultimate personal accolade, the Ballon d’Or.

Performances of several stars at the tournament have furthered their claims for the honour, with several Spain stars surging up the list of favourites after playing key roles in their triumph.

The Ballon d'Or will officially be announced on October 26.

Will there be a repeat winner or will a new name be on the honour roll for the third consecutive year?

Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the possible contenders to receive the prestigious prize.

Ousmane Dembele won last year's Ballon d'Or and is among the contenders again for the award

Harry Kane – 1/1

Heading up this list of possible winners is England captain and Bayern Munich’s No9, Harry Kane.

Kane has been at the peak of the footballing world for over a decade now, but has a serious chance of becoming the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or after the best statistical season of his career.

The 33-year-old scored a staggering 61 goals in 51 matches last season for Bayern Munich to help the German giants achieve a domestic double, as well as reaching a Champions League semi-final.

Despite Bayern falling to PSG in the last four, Kane scored in both legs of the semi-final, as he had also done against Real Madrid in the previous round.

Kane was equally brilliant for England in the World Cup, having been instrumental as Thomas Tuchel's side progressed to the semi-finals.

The England captain scored six goals, including two braces, but his lack of involvement in their semi-final loss to Argentina could count against him.

Historically just two domestic trophies would not be enough to win the Ballon d’Or but Kane’s mind-boggling output over the past year means he remains the bookies' favourite to win the prestigious prize.

Harry Kane could become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen

Lamine Yamal – 9/4

Kane will have his work cut out for him though, as the second on the list of favourites for this year’s award is Lamine Yamal.

The Barcelona and Spain star is seen as having a strong chance to become the first teenager to win the Ballon d’Or.

Since the start of last season, Yamal has been simply unstoppable. The Spaniard enjoyed a stellar season for both club and country, winning La Liga, the Spanish Super Cup and of course the World Cup.

Yamal racked up an impressive 16 goals and 12 assists in 28 La Liga games, while he also netted six times and assisted four goals in the Champions League.

His contribution would have likely been even higher had Yamal not seen the end of his season blighted by injury. He made a speedy recovery in time for the World Cup and while he may have not been at his blistering best, the winger played a vital role.

The 19-year-old, who started all but one game, was crucial to Spain’s success, despite only scoring one goal.

The threat he posed forced teams to double up on him, providing open space for teammates. Yamal was also expert in drawing free kicks and penalties through his trickery. Even with a low output his effect was still felt.

Spain's World Cup success has boosted Lamine Yamal's chances following on from his stunning season with Barcelona

Rodri – 9/2

Spain's World Cup winning captain Rodri has emerged as a leading contender following the tournament.

Rodri is an interesting case amongst this year’s favourites and presents the voters with a dilemma.

To many captaining your side to a World Cup with eight flawless performances should immediately make you a top candidate for the honour, but Rodri’s year has been disrupted by several injuries, preventing him from playing half of the Premier League season.

When on the pitch Rodri has been outstanding and he was deservedly named as the World Cup's Player of The Tournament after orchestrating sublime victories over France and Argentina in the semi-final and final respectively.

Victory for Rodri would indicate that performances in the biggest games are key, rather than consistency over the course of 12 months.

Rodri's starring role for Spain at the World Cup has pushed him into contention for the honour

The Spain captain was named as the World Cup's best player after their final triumph

Kylian Mbappe – 6/1

While French superstar Mbappe went another season without a trophy, his individual performances and numbers have been typically magnificent over the past nine months.

With Real Madrid, Mbappe netted an impressive 42 goals in 44 games, including 15 in 11 Champions League outings to end as the top scorer in the competition.

Mbappe was undoubtedly one of the leading figures at the World Cup, scoring ten goals to win the golden boot, finishing clear of his nearest challenger Lionel Messi.

The haul also saw Mbappe become the outright leading goalscorer in World Cup history.

Despite Mbappe reiterating his individual brilliance once again, a lack of silverware may hold him back from winning his first Ballon d’Or.

Kylian Mbappe secured the golden boot at the World Cup, but a lack of silverware my hold him back

Lionel Messi – 8/1

The timeless talent of Messi never seems to fade.

Messi, viewed by many as the greatest of all time, showed us this summer that he is far from finished and remains decisive on the world stage.

Despite Argentina losing the final, Messi's World Cup performances alone could bring him an extraordinary ninth Ballon d’Or.

Messi silenced doubters from the first match, in which he scored a hat-trick against Algeria. He would go on to contribute goals and assists in all but one of Argentina’s World Cup matches, racking up eight and four respectively.

While it may not hold as much weight as European domestic success, in late 2025 Messi spearheaded Inter Miami to their first ever MLS Cup victory, scoring six goals and getting seven assists in just six MLS play-off games.

Despite his advancing years, Messi was the inspiration behind Argentina's path to the World Cup final

Ousmane Dembele – 12/1

Reigning Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele is in contention for back-to-back triumphs.

After years of ridicule and derision in the early 2020s, Dembele has been transformed from an underachieving talent to the world’s best under Luis Enrique at PSG.

For the second year running, Dembele won the Champions League with the French side. The forward held his nerve to score their all-important equaliser from the penalty spot in the final against Arsenal – his 20th goal of the season.

Dembele also enjoyed a prolific World Cup with the Frenchman scoring six goals, including an excellent hat-trick against Norway. But his lack of influence in helping Les Bleus past Spain in their semi-final may count against him.

Ousmane Dembele helped PSG retain the Champions League, putting him in contention for back-to-back Ballon d'Or triumphs

Jude Bellingham – 14/1

Bellingham’s reputation was already stellar before this year, but he became England's Birmingham Baggio as he attempted to drive the Three Lions to the World Cup final, akin to how the ponytailed star had done for Italy in the 1994 tournament.

Similarly to his Madrid teammate Kylian Mbappe, Bellingham failed to pick up any silverware and will be massively held back by that in the voting. However, it would be ignorant to not at least consider Bellingham for the prize.

The midfielder certainly possesses the talent to deserve the prestigious award. However, the award rarely goes to the most gifted footballer at the time, but rather the most successful in that year’s campaign.

So unfortunately for Bellingham, despite his heroic England performances and unquestionable quality, a season in which you win no silverware and register 13 goals and assists in 40 games is unlikely to cut it.

Jude Bellingham starred for England at the World Cup to put him in contention for the award

Pau Cubarsi and Fabian Ruiz – 16/1 and 18/1

Two Spain stars from their World Cup triumph are viewed as outsiders for the prize.

Teenager defender Cubarsi was named as the Best Young Player at the World Cup, with Spain having conceded just one goal on their route to winning the tournament.

Cubarsi is joined by midfielder Fabian Ruiz, who has won both the World Cup and Champions League this year.

Despite getting fewer than ten goals and assists across the club season and the World Cup, Ruiz's contribution to his club and country’s success through his ability to keep and advance possession amongst other abilities has been invaluable.

Pau Cubarsi was named as the best young player at the World Cup after starring in defence for Spain

Fabian Ruiz won both the World Cup with Spain and the Champions League with PSG

Luis de la Fuente's decision to start him over Pedri in the latter stages of the World Cup and the performances that followed or his ability to stand out in a midfield with Joao Neves and Vitinha is a testament to his place in this list.

As across 1,131 minutes in Ligue one this past season Ruiz maintained a 91.5 per cent passing accuracy rate, was in the 99th percentile for progressive passes completed and the 82nd percentile for both key passes and chances created to other midfielders.

These performances alongside his trophy haul for the season make the Spaniard an outside shout for the award.

*Odds courtesy of SkyBet

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu is OUT of the US Open: British tennis star's horror run of injuries continues as doctors advise former champion to skip New York - hours after releasing video training in protective boot
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu is OUT of the US Open: British tennis star's horror run of injuries continues as doctors advise former champion to skip New York - hours after releasing video training in protective boot

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Emma Raducanu will miss the US Open as she continues to recover from the stress fracture which forced her to pull out of Wimbledon on the eve of the Championships.

It is a continuation of the British No1's dreadful run of injury and illness and - given the Open is the final Grand Slam of the year - her season is in danger of petering out.

The 23-year-old has been in St Moritz, Switzerland, from where she posted a video of herself practicing serves - with the significant caveat that she was still wearing a protective boot on her right leg.

And Daily Mail Sport understands that after her latest medical checks, the British No1 has been advised that the injury needs more time to heal and so she will be unable to contest the final Grand Slam of the season.

This latest issue is a continuation of a theme - since she won the US Open Raducanu has rarely been able to stay fit for a sustained period.

The lower-leg stress fracture - which first came to light when she was spotted leaving the All England Club in a protective boot in the week before Wimbledon - came on the back of a viral illness which laid her low for much of February through until May.

Emma Raducanu is set to miss the US Open later this month as her injury woes continue

The British No 1 had earlier shared a photo of her practicing in an orthopedic boot on Monday

Raducanu has been spending some of her rehab time in the high luxury of the Suvretta House hotel.

Opened in 1912 in the mountains of St Moritz, rooms can cost up to £2,500 a night.

The five-star hotel has a picturesque clay tennis court - upon which, it appears, Raducanu was unable to do much more than serving off one leg.

British tennis fans who follow and support Raducanu are used to disappointment but this recent run of illness and injury is particularly maddening given how well she has played during her brief periods of health.

In Cluj, Romania, and at the Queen's Club this year she made her first finals since the US Open title in 2021.

And her promising reunion with Andrew Richardson, the man who coached her to that miraculous Grand Slam title, is stuck in the starting blocks.

As ever, Raducanu's talent and athletic ability mean she is still capable of great things if she can stay fit. The problem is, with each passing year that 'if' becomes ever bigger.

Sports.title: Why Vinicius Junior IS worth the risk and the money for Arsenal: Better defensive numbers than you would think, how he would fit into Mikel Arteta's system and the link to Bruno Guimaraes signing
Sports.content:
It seems a bit silly, on the face of it, to even question why Mikel Arteta might want to sign one of the best players in the world.

Why wouldn’t he be keen to bring Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr to the Emirates Stadium in one of the biggest blockbuster moves in Premier League history – and especially when the Brazilian would fix the biggest flaw in Arsenal’s lop-sided attack?

It’s no secret that Arsenal relied far too much on its right flank last season, depended far too much on Bukayo Saka to conjure up some magic and, if that didn’t work, fell back on set-pieces to make up for it, while on the other wing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli never lacked in endeavour and industry but fell woefully short in output.

Arsenal ended the season as champions so perhaps we cannot complain too much but if Arteta wants to keep the Gunners on top of the mountain, and scale the one that has a Champions League trophy at its summit, he knows he needs to find a way to tip the scales back the other way.

Mikel Arteta is said to be highly enamoured with Vinicius Jr, but it will take a mammoth financial package to sign the Real Madrid man

Arteta knows Arsenal need an elite forward to go one step further and finally lift the European Cup for the first time in the club's 140-year history

Vinicius Jr would do that, and then some. The winger is one of the most dangerous ball carriers in world football. Even among the most elite dribblers across Europe’s Big Five Leagues, he stands alongside Barcelona sensation and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal as the very best.

Whenever he gets the ball at his feet, Vinicius Jr drives towards the box and either gets a shot away or, if you think you’ve closed the angle off, slips in his team-mate to get off one of their own.

No player created more chances after carrying the ball five metres or more across the Big Five Leagues last season than Vinicius Jr. The 49 shots he took himself after such carries was just one behind leader Yamal.

ALL COMPETITIONS, 2025-26 Player Games Goals Assists Total Vinicius Jr 53 22 14 36 Bukayo Saka 49 11 9 20 Leandro Trossard 50 8 11 19 Gabriel Martinelli 53 11 7 18 Noni Madueke 43 8 4 12

Saka is, by some distance, Arsenal’s best with the ball at his feet, but even his numbers are dwarfed by the staggering figures for Vinicius.

Trossard and Martinelli mustered just 19 shot-ending carries and 18 chance-ending ones between them.

Just a quick look at Vinicius Jr’s decisive carries shows how relentless and devastating he was at getting the ball, driving into the box and making things happen. Arsenal need more of those if they are to break down deep defences that often caused them problems last term.

No player created more chances after carrying the ball five metres or more across the Big Five Leagues last season than Vinicius Jr

He has scored in, and won, two Champions League finals in the last five seasons for Real Madrid

And yet, for all that brilliance, it’s impossible not to ignore that lingering doubt about whether he really is the right fit for Arsenal. Or, more specifically, for Arteta.

Spanish media outlet AS claimed that Arteta, in his bid to coax Vinicius Jr to north London, has promised to build his team around the Brazilian. Only, that goes against everything that has brought Arsenal glory under him.

So much of Arsenal’s success comes from their press and their teamwork in applying it together. They defend as a unit with everyone playing their part. If one part of the press doesn’t do its job, they are easy to play through.

As part of Daily Mail Sport’s analysis of why Arteta was so keen to sign Morgan Rogers, before they were gazumped by their rivals in blue down the road to the tune of £117million, we showed how a huge part of the allure in signing him was the defensive work Rogers did alongside his ability with the ball at his feet.

Not only did Rogers rank alongside Saka for joint-third most shot-ending carries in league last season but he also sat behind only the Arsenal winger for the most times any player won possession in the final third.

Even though his goals and assists were poor, no player with more than 500 minutes of league action averaged more ball recoveries in the final third than Martinelli.

Arteta wants his front line to be as busy without the ball as with it. You don’t get that with Vinicius Jr. Such demands have rarely been placed on him at Real Madrid either. Quite the opposite, in fact, where he has often been allowed to shirk those duties and focus on getting the most out of his devastating attacking qualities.

He wanders about the pitch, waiting for his colleagues to win the ball, then springs into action on the counter-attack. His perceived lack of effort saw Real fans turn on him frequently last season. ‘Work rate zero, tantrums 100’, was one cutting verdict after a shock home defeat to Getafe in which he preferred to gesture to the Bernabeu crowd instead of tracking back.

Vinicius showed his X factor at the World Cup, scoring four times in five matches

But for all his attacking prowess, Vinicius will be expected to do more defensively if he joins Arsenal

He won’t get such a free rein from Arteta, or the fans. If he does join – he returned to Real Madrid for pre-season training today – he will be expected to do his bit.

He’ll certainly have to do more than what he does already. Vinicius Jr won possession during matches far less than Saka, Martinelli or Trossard last term and nearly half as much in the final third as compatriot Martinelli.

DEFENSIVE DUTIES League games, 2025-26 Possession won Won in final third Duels won Bukayo Saka 4.7 1.1 6.8 Gabriel Martinelli 4.4 1.3 4.6 Vinicius Jr 2.8 0.7 6.3 Noni Madueke 2.6 0.7 5.6 Viktor Gyokeres 2.2 0.8 3.0 Kai Havertz 2.2 0.5 5.6

For all the grumbles, though, his numbers suggest there is room for improvement. He won possession high up the pitch about as often as Madueke. He won more duels – something Arteta values very highly – than all Arsenal forwards bar Saka.

His ball-winning figures from last term bettered those of Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres so, if Arteta is to build his team around him, then perhaps that opens up the possibility of Vinicius Jr playing up front, as he did frequently for Real and Brazil, especially in matches where Arteta wants to exploit space in behind.

Vinicius Jr did so in the Champions League last 16 second leg against Manchester City. Pep Guardiola’s side were 4-0 down on aggregate and chasing the game, leaving Vinicius Jr – playing as the central striker – the chance to break away as he did below. Despite scoring twice in the game, he raced through only to blaze his chance over the bar.

Vinicius bursts clear of the Manchester City defence, demonstrating how he could play as a central striker for Arteta

If Arteta is to make an exception on the pitch, he’ll have to make one off it too. It’s just that maybe, at the end of it all, he just thinks Vinicius is worth it

Arteta wants his team to play more of those passes to find more of those runs, and the potential arrival of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle would help unlock that.

That’s a definite option but that would still not fix the left-sided problem. Perhaps Arteta is willing to make a compromise: Know that Vinicius Jr won’t work as hard as Trossard or Martinelli but will more than make up for it with the weight of goals, assists and star power. If Arteta allows him to stay high up the pitch, it not only gives Arsenal the ideal out ball for a quick counter but will likely petrify opponents into leaving a player back to stop it.

Arteta maybe feels as though he has the players around Vinicius Jr to pick up the dirty work if left to do his thing. Again, if they land Guimaraes, his all-round, all-action ability would allow Arsenal's left-sided central midfielder, usually Declan Rice, to take on more of a clean-up role once Arsenal lose the ball.

Myles Lewis-Skelly would have the legs to cover the extra ground and the defensive nous that came from his time as a left-back. It might just mean Arsenal’s actual left-back, whether that be Riccardo Calafiori or Piero Hincapie, might have to resist any urges to bomb forward on the overlap.

Vinicius Jr’s arrival would also shatter Arsenal’s balanced wage structure. He’s a superstar that would come with a superstar salary. If Arteta is to make an exception on the pitch, he’ll have to make one off it too. It’s just that maybe, at the end of it all, he just thinks he’s worth it.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn makes seven-figure demand for latest star but admits he 'might not be the best'
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn makes seven-figure demand for latest star but admits he 'might not be the best'

England and Northampton star Henry Pollock is now managed by Matchroom and Eddie Hearn - who is seeking a record pay day for the player's next contract

View 2 Images Eddie Hearn is handling Henry Pollock's contract talks

Eddie Hearn has claimed that Northampton star Henry Pollock is "a seven-figure player" as he goes into contract talks with Northampton - even if the promoter admits "there might be players who are better".

‌



Pollock opted to join up with the Matchroom supremo several months ago and now has Hearn leading his contract negotiations with the Prem champions. The 21-year-old’s contract is thought to be around £150,000 per year, but it expires at the end of next season.

‌



Hearn is looking to land the England back rower a bumper pay day and has told Northampton to "recognise what they have got" whilst he stated that Pollock was "making an unquestionable difference to the bottom line of the club."

‌



The Matchroom chief is a hugely influential figure and has talked up the money Pollock could get if he chose to move elsewhere - and his financial demands would make Pollock comfortably the highest paid player at Franklin's Gardens.

Lewis Moody health latest as star arrives at Wimbledon after MND diagnosis READ MORE :

England strategy in the spotlight as Prem's best leaves and Exeter boss spells out reality READ MORE :

Hearn told the Telegraph: “It is all very well saying that there might be players who are a bit more consistent or might be better or whatever, but there aren’t players that are making an unquestionable and undeniable difference to the bottom line of the club.

‌



“Henry Pollock drives season ticket sales. Henry Pollock puts bums on the seats. Henry Pollock drives viewership on TNT or wherever it’s going to be. Henry Pollock sells shirts, right? That’s the difference. So you can actually put an economic value over having Henry Pollock on the team, and that has to be recognised, regardless of the want from Henry. He cannot stay at this club on the money that he’s on.”

Alongside his Northampton contract Pollock also receives around £150,000 per year from the Rugby Football Union as an enhanced elite player squad member with England. Northampton though have spent under the £6.4m cap with their marquee player thought to be fly-half Fin Smith.

View 2 Images Henry Pollock was recently with Eddie Hearn on his yacht (Image: @henryjpollock)

Article continues below

Reports claim Tommy Freeman will soon pen a deal that makes him the Prem's best paid winger but Hearn has talked up Pollock's financial pull off the pitch, even if the player would like to remain at Northampton. He also claimed the club's opening offer was not a “fair representation of his commercial value”.

“The first thing I said to Henry was: ‘Do you want to stay at Northampton?’” Hearn said. “And he said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘I love the club, I love the team, I love that I live 10 minutes away, and I think we’re going to win the championship again next year and I want to win championships'."

If Pollock wants to remain playing for England, which is the case, then he will have to sign with a club in the Prem. Many of those are already spending close to the cap and few would have the scope to pay a player £1m as things stand.

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu OUT of US Open as injury nightmare continues for British No.1
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu OUT of US Open as injury nightmare continues for British No.1

Emma Raducanu has been forced to skip the US Open due to a stress fracture in her lower right leg, having missed Wimbledon earlier in the summer

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu has been hampered by injuries recently (Image: Getty)

Emma Raducanu will miss a second consecutive Grand Slam tournament as she continues to recover from a stress fracture in her lower right leg.

‌



The world No. 49 is set to skip the US Open after pulling out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament earlier this summer.

‌



Raducanu, 23, has not played a match since finishing runner-up at the Queen’s Club almost two months ago. It’s now been five years since the Brit made history at the US Open, becoming the first and only qualifier to win a Major title.

‌



But on the half-decade anniversary of her heroic run, she will not compete in Flushing Meadows.

The US Open gets underway in less than four weeks, but Raducanu has already decided to skip the event on medical advice and is said to be sad to miss such a special tournament.

Since pulling out of Wimbledon, the British No. 1 has been spotted wearing a protective boot on her right leg. She has also shared footage from some early practice sessions. One video showed Raducanu sitting on a bin and hitting balls. In a second clip, filmed during a trip to Switzerland, she stood on a clay court and hit some serves.

‌



The US Open concludes on September 13, by which time Raducanu won’t have played a match for three months. She was also not named in Britain’s squad for the Billie Jean King Finals, which takes place in Shenzhen from September 22 to 27.

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu withdrew from Wimbledon less than 24 hours before her first round match (Image: Getty)

The world No. 49 also missed more than two months of competition from March to May due to post-viral illness, while a bone bruising injury in her foot wrecked her pre-season preparations. And the stress fracture is the latest issue to derail Raducanu’s 2026 season.

Article continues below

Announcing her withdrawal from Wimbledon on the night before her first-round match this summer, she said: “I can’t believe I’m saying this, but sadly I’ve had to withdraw from this year’s Wimbledon.

“I’ve done everything possible to try to get to the start line tomorrow but after a final scan tonight, the niggle I’ve been managing has developed into a stress fracture and I’ve been medically advised to stop pushing through.

“Playing at Wimbledon, in front of a home crowd, means everything to me, so this is really difficult to process. I want to thank you all for your support and encouragement. Especially at a time like this, it is invaluable. I look forward to seeing you when I’m back.”

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to battle Barcelona for £13.7m star as they establish transfer plan B
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to battle Barcelona for £13.7m star as they establish transfer plan B

Manchester United are looking to make additions at left-back and, should they miss out on Newcastle's Lewis Hall, then they could battle Barcelona for Spanish teenager Jorge Salinas

View 2 Images Man Utd have been keeping tabs on highly rated Spanish teenager Jorge Salinas

Manchester United are reportedly considering a move for Racing Santander full-back Jorge Salinas, who is their back-up option should they miss out on Lewis Hall.

‌



The Newcastle star is on the club's shortlist and the Magpies have already seen a number of their leading lights leave this summer. Bruno Guimaraes is being pursued by Arsenal and could follow Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali out the door with the club into a period of transition.

‌



Eddie Howe has just called time on his five-year tenure and United are looking to seize on the uncertainty around the club by going after Hall, who has continued to blossom since moving to St James' Park from Chelsea.

‌



Newcastle are in no hurry to cash in on Hall and would demand an offer in excess of £50million before they even considered letting the England international leave - which has left United having to look elsewhere.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut READ MORE :

And Spanish newspaper SPORT claim that Santander’s Salinas has emerged as a target. The club hold a genuine interest in the 19-year-old, but if he does move on then his preference is thought to be a move to Barcelona. He played a key role last season as his boyhood team won promotion to La Liga.

‌



As it stands the Red Devils are prepared to pay Salinas’ €16m (£13.7m) release clause, but it remains to be seen how willing the player himself is to make the move. Barcelona see Salinas as a replacement for Joao Cancelo, who is set to make the move to Saudi Pro League outfit Al-Hilal.

United have been keeping close tabs on Salinas and were impressed by his performances at this summer’s European Under-19 Championship, where Spain claimed the trophy.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall has been heavily linked with Man Utd (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Article continues below

United's first choice left-back is Luke Shaw and the ex-Southampton man has been an impressive and consistent performer, but fitness has been an issue throughout his career and the versatile defender is now 31.

Already this summer United have signed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos with bolstering their midfield a priority for the Red Devils. They could yet add more quality in that area but left-back is also an area that had been cited as somewhere they could improve their squad.
