World.title: Sititi tips De Villiers as tour threat while fighting his own way back into All Blacks’ Test plans
World.content:
Wallace Sititi has praised Springbok flanker Paul de Villiers ahead of the Greatest Rivalry tour while working to regain his own Test spot.

All Blacks loose forward Wallace Sititi has singled out Springbok youngster Paul de Villiers as a player to watch during the Castle Double Malt Greatest Rivalry tour, even as he himself battles to force his way back into the All Blacks’ Test starting lineup.

Asked about the 23-year-old Stormers flanker who has taken the Springbok environment by storm this season, Sititi did not hold back.



“Big boy,” he said. “He loves the collision battle. Good over the ball. He’s a quality footy player,”

“Hopefully we’ll be able to see him a couple of times throughout this tour,” Sititi said at a media session ahead of Friday’s tour opener against the Stormers.

It is high praise from a fellow loose forward who knows exactly what it takes to function at the breakdown in the Test arena. De Villiers has featured in every Springbok match-day squad this season – the only recent debutant to achieve that distinction – completing 16 tackles and eight carries against Scotland while earning rave reviews from World Cup winners Bakkies Botha and Kwagga Smith.

His low body position at the jackal and his ability to slow ball at the breakdown has drawn comparisons to Heinrich Brüssow, the breakdown specialist who tormented the All Blacks decades ago.

SITITI LOOKING FOR A WAY BACK INTO THE TEST FOLD

For Sititi, the acknowledgement of De Villiers’ quality comes against a personal backdrop of genuine challenge. The Kiwi flank, who made his Test debut in Cape Town two years ago, has had a difficult run of form due injury-related issues and finds himself currently outside the Test selection picture under new coach Dave Rennie.

“All Blacks is a high-performance environment that expects the best,” Sititi said plainly. “When you don’t play your best, they get someone to do it because there’s a lot of quality out here. Obviously, it’s tough. But at the same time, we support each other.”



Asked whether he has a clear roadmap back into Test contention, Sititi kept his answer refreshingly simple. “I’m just trying to enjoy the footy,” he said. “When I play my best, I feel like that’s the focus too.”

The midweek tour fixtures against the Stormers, Sharks, Bulls and Lions offer Sititi that exact platform.

“Those mid-week games against the Super franchises, we treat it like it’s a Test match,” he said. “We know what the quality is like here. At the same time, it’s an opportunity. We just love playing footy.”

World.title: Alexandra drowning in rubbish
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - There is no light at the end of the tunnel for Pikitup’s escalating waste crisis.

The gridlock has now hit Alexandra, where a strike by casual workers has ground collections to a halt, turning local streets into sprawling, illegal dumping grounds.

Residents say they’re being forced to live among mounds of rubbish with no end to the health hazard in sight.

"We don’t have a municipality anymore. In fact, in the municipality, we just have criminals who are thinking about themselves. So that’s why they don’t care..."one resident said.

Community leader Thabo Mopasi said the conditions have become unacceptable.

"We are not pleased, it’s now election time and we are going through rubble like this and rubbish like this. There are rodents all over, it’s chaotic and it’s a health hazard..." Mopasi said.

The disruptions stem from ongoing protest action by casual workers demanding permanent employment.

The entrances to some depots like Randburg and Waterval, have been blocked again, further disrupting refuse collection.

Pikitup has repeatedly said it’s working to restore normal services and clear the backlog. But weeks into the dispute, the impasse with striking workers remains unresolved.

eNCA’s Nabeelah Shaikh filed this report.

World.title: Water tanker becomes centre of deadly tragedy in KZN
World.content:
DURBAN - The City of eThekwini Mayor, Cyril Xaba, has described the incident in which a water tanker drove over and killed a resident in uMbumbulu as a tragic accident.

Xaba said they cannot speculate on the circumstances surrounding the incident, and as such, have handed the matter over to law enforcement for further probe.

"The police will assist with the matter and from there we will await the findings in this regard.”

The 39-year-old man was knocked over by the tanker, causing fatal injuries.

Witnesses claim the tanker continued moving and did not stop immediately after the incident.

The incident has turned the spotlight to water woes in the city.

According to Xaba, the area has long been riddled by water outages; as such, the community is serviced by water tankers and boreholes to ensure that households receive water.

In addressing the issue, he said the city is working on a R1.2 billion Southern Aqueduct project, which is a 24-kilometre pipeline aimed at improving water to areas including Shallcross, Chatsworth, uMlazi, Folweni and Queensburgh.

World.title: Tension at Kamukunji Police Station as leaders demand Kaguchia's release
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Mukuruwe-ini MP John Kaguchia at Kamukunji Police Station in Nairobi on August 3, 2026. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Tension is high at Kamukunji Police Station as opposition leaders led by Kipipiri MP Wanjiku Muhia and lawyers demand the immediate release of Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia, claiming police had failed to comply with a High Court order granting him police cash bail.

Kaguchia, who was arrested earlier on Monday over alleged electoral offences and incitement, remained in police custody hours after his lawyers said the court had ordered his release on Sh100,000 police bail.

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua in a post on his Facebook account said that the High Court had issued orders directing the Officer Commanding Station (OCS) at Kamukunji Police Station to release the legislator immediately upon payment of the bail.

Gachagua said that despite the court order having been served, the OCS had not acted and was instead awaiting instructions from his superiors. He warned the officer against disobeying a court order, saying that he could be held personally liable for contempt of court if the directive was ignored.

The former Deputy President further referenced the ongoing murder case involving the former OCS of Central Police Station, urging police officers to uphold the law and avoid carrying out unlawful instructions.

Several Members of Parliament from the Mt Kenya region have camped outside Kamukunji Police Station, insisting they would not leave until Kaguchia is released. The legislators accused police of delaying compliance with the court order and questioned why the MP was still being held despite the court's directive.

The lawmakers that claimed they had been redirected to Central Police Station while seeking information about Kaguchia's detention.

Kaguchia's arrest has sparked political debate, with opposition leaders accusing investigative agencies of selectively enforcing the law against government critics. They argue that other leaders who have previously made controversial public statements have not faced similar action.

World.title: Why Kenyans' trust gap on IEBC continues to grow
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC is gaining mistrust among Kenyans. [File, Standard]

The reconstituted Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) assumed office about a year ago on the backdrop of growing mistrust among Kenyans.

But, even before it conducts its first General Elections, the Commission is already confronting a fresh credibility test after proposing restrictions on the livestreaming of election results.

The proposal, presented as part of efforts to safeguard the integrity of the tallying process, has instead reignited long-standing public anxieties over transparency in the country's electoral management system.

For many Kenyans, whose confidence in election management has been repeatedly shaken by disputed presidential results, court battles and allegations of manipulation, the move has reinforced fears that access to real-time information could be curtailed at the most critical stage of the democratic process.

The government sponsored Bill, whose fate now lies with the National Assembly, is jointly sponsored by Senate Majority leader Aaron Cheruiyot and Minority leader Stewart Madzayo.

The Bill that has stalled at the First Reading level in the Assembly since February 2024, seeks to repeal section 39(1)(g) of the Elections Act.

If approved, live transmission of results displayed by the Commission at the National Tallying Centre may not be there in the 2027 polls.

Kenyans have since responded to the proposal, pouring their anger and outrage as they question the motive behind the proposal, with some suggesting that the move could be introduced to conceal ill motives during elections.

"No doubt this is exactly what the IEBC fears; a transparent electoral process that every Kenyan can verify,' Wabowoba Calwo said on X in a post accompanied by a clip where an individual is seen pointing at a screen livestreaming the recently conducted Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election.

"Kenyans must demand nothing less than a free and fair 2027 election," he added, asserting that "transparency is not going to be a favour by anybody, it is a democratic safeguard."

According to another user, banning of real-time live streaming of election results would undermine the integrity of polls and create anxiety among voters.

"If the IEBC fails to livestream the General Election, it will create unnecessary suspicion, undermine transparency and provide fertile ground for claims of electoral malpractice," he posted.

According to Yamine, an X user, live broadcasts of election results keep Kenyans informed. promote transparency, provide a clear picture of the voting process, and help ease tension rather than "fuel uncertainty."

"In real democracies, results are streamed live so every citizen can watch and decide for themselves," posted Yamine.

Alfred Abuya said :"I strongly reject this move. Why will they even imagine doing something like counting votes in the dark? Are they working for someone or independent forces behind the idea?"

However, IEBC has since denied claims that the proposed law seeks to scrap the live transmission of election results, saying they have been misunderstood.

In a statement on Thursday, the Commission said the Bill does not amend Section 44 of the Elections Act, which provides for the Integrated Elections Management System used for Voter registration.

It argued, instead, that the amendment is envisioned to introduce an alternative transmission mechanism for areas without the minimum 3G network required to electronically transmit results.

The Commission further said it will still be required to verify results by comparing the original physical Form 34A with its electronically submitted results.

"The Bill seeks to align the law with the Supreme Court's decision in Presidential Election Petition No 1 of 20217, which affirmed that the election result is one recorded in the statutory Results Declaration Form (Form 34A Series), the primary and final record of the results at the polling station," said the commission.

According to youth activist Allans Ademba who mobilised the "Tuko Kadi" mass voter registration call, the move will erode public trust in the agency.

"If IEBC wants to win the trust of youths, it must ensure credible results. This can only happen if they allow live streaming," he said, adding that "apart from malicious forms which the commission can manage, there was no need to ban it."

Appearing on a local TV show early this week, nominated MP Sabina Chege, said the electoral agency was yet to justify to Kenyans what informed such a decision.

"The IEBC has not provided any justification for mending the live streaming of elections," she said.

Former National Assembly Speaker Justin Muturi has also criticised the proposal, terming it retrogressive and an outright attack on democracy and the rule of law.

"Any proposal from whichever quarter to ban the live streaming of election results is not only unconstitutional and offensive to the principles of open governance, but also a stain on the democratic conscience of the Kenyan people," he said.

He said "Darkness and democracy are not synonymous. Transparency is the life -blood of free, fair and credible elections."

Appearing on Spice Fm morning show on Thursday, Lawyer Ndegwa Njiru said: "Our Constitution is built on the principles of transparency, accountability and the participation of the people. Election results are not the property of the IEBC, they belong to Kenyans.

World.title: CS sued in bid to kick out Railways boss, audit SGR contracts
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

A court battle is brewing over Kenya Railways operations and the corporation’s Managing Director Phillip Mainga's reign.

A petitioner is now seeking to push the KR boss out, claiming he is employed on permanent terms.

In the case against KR board, the Attorney General and Transport Cabinet Secretary, the complainant alleges that Mainga was appointed in 2018, noting that State corporations hire their bosses on short-term contracts.

Mainga has been named as an interested party.

“Under the prevailing governance principles applicable to the state corporations, the office of the Managing Director is not meant to be occupied indefinitely,” argues Wahome Mucunu, adding that Mainga’s tenure in office ought to have allegedly lapsed in 2024.

Mucunu claims that the corporation has been at the heart of numerous concerns over procurement and transparency.

He states that among the projects that have raised concerns are the Standard Gauge Railway (SGR project).

According to him, Transparency International this year in March this year allegedly indicated that SGR was a high-risk project, with a 4.9 out of 5 corruption risk score.

“The project has equally generated sustained public debate concerning transparency, accountability, value for money, public participation, procurement practices and debt sustainability. The Petitioner states that the people of Kenya, being the ultimate financiers of the project through taxation and public borrowing, possess a legitimate constitutional interest in the manner in which the project was conceived, procured, financed and implemented,” says Muchunu.

He further claims that Transparency International indicated that public institutions, among them KR, allegedly repeatedly failed to provide information requested by accountability actors and researchers. Muchunu alleged that the assessment concluded that the responses received were insufficient to facilitate effective public oversight.

“All material times relevant to this Petition, the first interested party, Mr. Phillip Mainga, has served as the Managing Director of Kenya Railways Corporation. The office of Managing Director constitutes the highest executive office within the Corporation and carries overall responsibility for the administration, management and operational control of the affairs of the Corporation,” he argues.

He also claims that many questions have been raised by members of the public, civil society organisations, governance experts and accountability institutions regarding the management of major projects undertaken by the corporation.

According to him, the answers given do not allegedly exude confidence as they are not allegedly fully addressed.

“Such concerns have centered on the adequacy of procurement procedures, transparency of contractual arrangements, disclosure of project costs and effectiveness of oversight mechanisms. The Petitioner states that these concerns have never been adequately addressed in a manner capable of restoring public confidence,” he continues.

In his case before Justice David Mburu, the petitioner urges the court to find that failure to disclose details about the SGR contract was a violation of the Constitution. He also seeks for a finding that Mainga ought to have left office by last year.

At the same time, he is urging the court to rule that the parastatal’s board had violated the Constitution and to compel it to find his successor.

Muchunu also wants to have the SGR project contracts audited.

World.title: Tiktoker Mauti changes plea, freed on bail in case involving Ruto's children
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

TikToker Hesbon Mauti was charged for posting a video threatening to kill and defile President William Ruto's children. [Nancy Gitonga, Standard]

TikToker Hesbon Mauti Thomas, accused of posting a video containing remarks threatening President William Ruto’s son George Ruto and daughter, has been released on a Sh5,000 cash bail after changing his plea to not guilty.

Mauti appeared before Milimani Principal Magistrate Geoffrey Onsarigo on Friday, July 31, 2026, where the charge of offensive conduct conducive to breaches of the peace was read afresh to him.

The accused, who had initially pleaded guilty to the charge on Thursday, changed his plea after his lawyer Cliff Ombeta applied for the matter to be reopened and for the charge to be read again.

The court allowed the application, after which Mauti denied the charge and pleaded not guilty.

According to the charge sheet, Mauti is accused of posting a video on June 25, 2026, through his TikTok account PROVIDENT@bonifaceaminga, containing remarks that prosecutors say were likely to cause a breach of the peace.

The charge sheet alleges that Mauti altered words in the video to make remarks targeting President Ruto’s son George Ruto and his daughter, while demanding that their parents be paid Sh2 million.

Mauti is charged with offensive conduct conducive to breaches of the peace contrary to Section 94(1) of the Penal Code, Chapter 63 of the Laws of Kenya.

After denying the charges, his defence team told the court that Mauti is a young man and a law student at Chuka University whose fees are paid by a church.

The lawyers further informed the court that Mauti is an orphan and has no parents to assist him in securing his release, asking the court to grant him a lenient cash bail.

“We are looking at the charges and when we look at it and the consequences that come from that, and if it goes on this particular way we know what the sentence is and what the consequences are. The court has got the right before passing the sentence to be able to reconsider when he changes his plea,” his lawyers told the court.

The defence also told the court that they had advised Mauti that the earlier position he had taken by pleading guilty carried serious consequences and offered to represent him in the matter.

The prosecution did not oppose his release on bail.

Magistrate Onsarigo granted Mauti a cash bail of Sh5,000 and directed him to provide one contact person.

The matter will be mentioned on August 18, 2026, for pre-trial directions.

World.title: Ruto calls for national dialogue to shape Kenya's vision
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Ruto said recent economic reforms had laid a stronger foundation for future growth. [File, Standard]

President William Ruto has invited Kenyans to take part in what he described as the country's most significant national conversation since the adoption of the 2010 Constitution, saying the discussions will help chart Kenya's next long-term development agenda.

Speaking on the country's development trajectory, the President said the conversation should move beyond partisan politics and election cycles to focus on a shared national vision.

"I invite every Kenyan to what I believe will become the most consequential national conversation since the adoption of our Constitution in 2010," Ruto said.

"A national conversation about Kenya's development. This conversation must rise above politics, transcend electoral cycles and unite us around a shared destiny."

The President acknowledged that while Vision 2030 had set an ambitious goal of transforming Kenya into an upper-middle-income country by 2030, the country remains off course to achieve that target.

"Vision 2030 set a target of Kenya becoming an upper-middle-income country by 2030. So far, we are off target. This is not a criticism of Vision 2030, nor is it a reason for disappointment; rather, it is an opportunity to learn from our successes proudly, reflect with honesty on where we have fallen short, and define together Kenya's next long-term vision," he said.

At the same time, Ruto announced that the government will formally launch a nationwide conversation on August 12 to develop Kenya's next long-term development blueprint as Vision 2030 nears its end.

"Accordingly, on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, we shall formally launch the National Conversation on Kenya's Future Beyond Vision 2030; the most consequential exercise in national reflection and public participation since the promulgation of our Constitution in 2010," he stated.

Ruto said recent economic reforms had laid a stronger foundation for future growth, citing improvements in key macroeconomic indicators.

"We have stabilized our currency, inflation has fallen, borrowing costs have declined, and investor confidence has returned," he said. "Last year Kenya attracted a record $3.2 billion in foreign direct investment, more than double the amount recorded in 2022."

He added that Kenya's improving investment climate had earned international recognition.

"The 2025 IMD World Competitiveness Ranking placed Kenya as the most competitive economy in Africa, reflecting the confidence our reforms have restored," Ruto said.

At the same time, Ruto also highlighted the establishment of the National Infrastructure Fund and the Sovereign Wealth Fund, saying the two institutions would help finance strategic investments while safeguarding the country's wealth for future generations.

According to Ruto, Kenya must now confront difficult questions about its development path to unlock its full potential.

"The question we must ask ourselves candidly and honestly is why other nations have fulfilled so much of their potential while we have repeatedly fallen short. What must we now do differently to ensure that the next chapter of Kenya's development story is fundamentally different from the last?" he posed.

He urged all Kenyans to help shape a new long-term national vision, saying the country's future depends on collective commitment rather than political divisions.

World.title: Lawyer seeks orders to suspend court boycott
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Advocate Adrian Kamotho argues that LSK's actions create the impression that court orders can be overturned through a boycott. [File, Standard]

A city lawyer has moved to the High Court seeking conservatory orders to suspend the Law Society of Kenya's (LSK) ongoing targeted boycott of judges and judicial officers.

In a petition filed under a certificate of urgency, Advocate Adrian Kamotho has sued LSK led by President Charles Kanjama, over its nationwide and targeted court boycott of Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Philomena Mwilu and other judges, arguing that the action is unconstitutional, undermines judicial independence and denies litigants access to justice.

"The LSK's actions create the impression that lawful court orders can be overturned through a boycott, setting a dangerous precedent to the rule of law and thereby undermining the proper administration of justice," Kamotho states in the petition.

The lawyer has named the Judicial Service Commission (JSC), Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Mwilu, several Supreme Court, High Court and Environment and Land Court judges, Court of Appeal Judge Sankale Ole Kantai, Kibera Chief Magistrate Stella Atambo and the Kenya Magistrates and Judges Association as interested parties in the case.

He is seeking orders to immediately suspend the implementation of the LSK's targeted boycott announced through statements and operational guidelines issued on July 17, July 20 and July 22, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the petition.

"Pending the hearing and determination of this Petition, the court be pleased to issue a conservatory order restraining the LSK, whether by itself, its Council, officers, agents or any person acting under its authority, from implementing, enforcing or giving effect to the targeted boycott," Kamotho seeks.

According to the petition, the targeted boycott, which commenced on July 23, directs advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before judges listed by the LSK.

East Africa Law Society president Ramadhan Abubakar Mukira addresses the media on the court boycott outside the Supreme Court of Kenya in Nairobi on July 22, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Lawyers are also required to seek adjournments, transfers or recusals of matters regardless of their clients' instructions.

"The Respondent has directed advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before the listed judges and judicial officers," Kamotho states.

He adds: "Advocates appearing before the targeted judges and judicial officers have been directed to seek the transfer, recusal or adjournment of pending proceedings, irrespective of their clients' instructions, the circumstances of the individual case or the applicable legal principles."

Kamotho further claims the society has threatened disciplinary action against judges, judicial officers and advocates who decline to implement the boycott.

"The LSK has further directed that any judge, judicial officer or advocate who declines to facilitate the boycott be reported to it for 'appropriate action,' including possible complaints before the Judicial Service Commission and such further action as its Council may deem necessary," he says.

According to the petition, every day the boycott remains in force exposes court users to delayed justice and unnecessary hardship.

"Every day that the targeted boycott remains operative exposes litigants and court users to adjournments, disruption of part-heard proceedings, expiry of interim protection measures, prolonged detention, additional expense and denial or delay of access to justice," Kamotho argues.

He also faults the LSK for allegedly including the late Supreme Court Judge Mohammed Ibrahim in its list of judges affected by the boycott.

"The targeted list of judges includes Hon. Justice Mohammed Ibrahim (deceased), demonstrating unconscionable casualness on the part of the LSK and apparent failure to verify elementary material facts before imposing measures of such gravity," the petition states.

Kamotho contends that the boycott creates an unlawful mechanism for exerting pressure on judges outside the constitutional framework.

He argues that the dispute raises fundamental constitutional questions, including whether the LSK has the legal authority to organise an indefinite boycott, compel advocates to withhold legal services from clients and determine which judicial functions judges may perform.

He maintains that the boycott threatens litigants' constitutional rights to equality before the law, access to justice, legal representation and a fair hearing, particularly in urgent and criminal matters.

In his supporting affidavit, Kamotho says advocates have been placed in an impossible position by the LSK's directives.

"The directions therefore place advocates in an immediate and irreconcilable conflict between their lawful professional duties and the Respondent's threatened enforcement measures," he says.

He further says litigants are innocent parties caught in an institutional dispute.

"The practical burden of the boycott consequently falls upon litigants and court users who are strangers to the institutional dispute forming the alleged basis of the boycott," he states.

Kamotho insists the conservatory orders sought are intended only to preserve uninterrupted court operations and judicial independence pending determination of the constitutional petition, arguing that the public interest favours continued access to courts and legal representation rather than disruption of judicial proceedings.

The petition is pending directions and hearing.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: This is not the first time Trump has called off strikes on Iran
World.content:
US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that he called off planned strikes on Iran, adding later that officials from Washington and Tehran will meet for talks later today. Iran has denied it is having discussions with the US.

This is not the first time during the conflict that Trump has threatened attacks then called them off.

World.title: Anthropic said its AI models hacked into other companies’ systems during testing
World.content:
AI company Anthropic says that during routine testing some of its models accessed the internet and hacked into three separate organizations’ systems – and that it didn’t notice the models had done so until an internal review prompted by rival OpenAI disclosing its models did the same.

Anthropic said in an announcement on Thursday that it started a review of its own systems after OpenAI disclosed last week that during a cybersecurity test some of its models escaped their testing environment, accessed the open internet and hacked into AI platform Hugging Face’s systems.

Anthropic said it found three instances where its AI models accessed the open internet when they were not supposed to and “gained unauthorized access to the production infrastructure of three different organizations.” The company said it discovered the incidents while reviewing more than 140,000 evaluations following OpenAI’s disclosure. Like during OpenAI’s tests, normal safety guardrails were removed during Anthropic’s evaluations to assess their models’ full capabilities.

Anthropic explained that in the three instances its models were given a fake “capture the flag” challenge, told that the “flag” was hidden on a different machine on the network and that its objective was to break in and retrieve it. Unlike OpenAI’s situation, Anthropic said none of its models deliberately attempted to escape their testing environments. Instead what happened was that the models were not supposed to have access to the open internet but that they were able to due to a misunderstanding between Anthropic and its evaluation partner, the company said in its statement.

To break into the three unnamed organizations, the models used basic techniques like “exploiting weak passwords” and finding system points that do not require log ins or tokens, Anthropic said. The most advanced version of its models did at some point recognize it was on the open internet, and stopped itself from continuing, the company said.

Anthropic said the earliest incident of its models breaching another organization was from April, and that none of the organizations recognized they had been hacked. Anthropic said they are in the process of working with the organizations affected.

OpenAI’s disclosure of its models hacking Hugging Face shook the cybersecurity and AI worlds, as it was the first real world example of something experts had long warned about: AI agents with advanced cybersecurity skills escaping testing environments and causing real-world harm.

Like OpenAI, Anthropic said on Thursday it has stopped all cyber evaluations. Anthropic acknowledged it could have taken more “in-depth” measures to prevent the cybersecurity breaches from happening.

Anthropic’s disclosure further confirms that AI agents unintentionally hacking other organizations is not limited to one AI company, and will likely further amplify calls for better AI testing safeguards and tools to potentially slow down AI development that may be moving much faster than society is ready for.

World.title: Deadly bomb explosion at Moscow restaurant was ‘terrorist attack,’ mayor says
World.content:
Moscow’s mayor says a bomb blast that killed at least two people and injured 21 others at a restaurant was a “terrorist attack.”

An unidentified woman attempted to enter a private event at the Balzi Rossi restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square carrying what authorities believe was an improvised explosive device, state media reported. The bomb went off before she entered, killing the security guard who stopped her, and a customer, as well as the woman carrying the device, according to authorities.

Authorities did not immediately identify the woman and it was also unclear whether she deliberately detonated the device.

Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, “Yesterday, a brutal terrorist attack took place in Moscow, claiming the lives of several people.”

“Those responsible for this crime will certainly be found and will face the punishment they deserve,” he added, giving no details on a motive or who might be behind the attack.

Pro-Kremlin REN TV reported that two of the victims taken to hospital had since died from their injuries, citing a source. This has not been confirmed by officials.

The apparent targets were guests attending a private event on the restaurant’s outdoor terrace, Russian business daily Kommersant reported. Sources told the newspaper that the event was heavily guarded, which may have prevented a significantly higher death toll.

Kommersant said a security guard became suspicious of a courier approaching with a box she described as a gift and decided to search her. The device exploded at that moment.

Investigators believe the bomb was detonated remotely, and a preliminary account indicates that the woman most likely did not know what the package contained, Kommersant reported.

The device had the explosive force of one kilogram of TNT and was packed with metal ball bearings intended to increase casualties, according to the newspaper.

While Russian authorities have not alleged a Ukraine link as of yet, Moscow has previously blamed Kyiv for a series of assassinations or assassination attempts on high-profile military officials since the war.

The blast happened around 8:10 p.m. local time (1:10 p.m. ET) near the outdoor terrace, according to Russian state news agency TASS, which cited the Main Directorate of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. The restaurant is located at the base of a landmark tower on Kudrinskaya Square, one of Moscow’s famous “Seven Sisters,” a group of Stalinist skyscrapers built in the 1950s.

The explosion immediately prompted the deployment of an investigative task force and a large number of police and emergency personnel to the site, which sits along the Garden Ring in Moscow’s central Presnensky district.

The restaurant said it was “deeply saddened by the tragedy and extends its sincere condolences to the families and loved ones of those who were killed.”

The nature of the attack has prompted widespread speculation over who might have been targeted.

The attack bore similarities to a 2023 bombing that killed a pro-war blogger, Vladlen Tatarsky. In that incident a woman was ‌jailed for ​27 years ​for delivering a bomb concealed inside a statuette that exploded in Tatarsky’s hands.

World.title: Iran appears indifferent to latest Trump talk on negotiations
World.content:
US President Donald Trump spoke optimistically at the weekend about a resumption of negotiations with Iran and prospects for a swift agreement on the Strait of Hormuz, the issue at the heart of the stop-start conflict.

But according to the language and tone from Tehran Monday, Iran is not talking with the United States and feels no need to, and is rather focused on a bilateral deal with Oman on how to manage the critical waterway.

“To avoid any ambiguity, it should be clarified who the negotiations are with. We currently have no negotiations with the United States; the negotiations are with Oman,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said.

And they would not lead automatically to a reopening of the strait, he added.

“This agreement (with Oman) is solely about the mechanism and future shipping route while preserving the sovereign rights of both countries and has no connection to whether the Strait of Hormuz is open or closed.

That route, according to Baghaei, would be temporary, serving the “interests of both coastal states.” It would be a single corridor, rather than two routes – one close to the Iranian coast and one close to Oman’s – that had been discussed previously.

“Whether this stage and this process can be connected to another process that leads to a reduction of tensions in the region, we must wait and see,” Baghaei said.

Tehran is essentially saying that it’s oblivious to Trump’s remarks and blames the United States for blowing up the Memorandum of Understanding agreed in June.

“It violated all of its commitments, reinstated the illegal maritime blockade, revoked the authorization for the sale of Iranian oil, and effectively declared almost all of the other commitments it had accepted under the memorandum null and void,” Baghaei said.

While that remained the case, he asserted, “naturally no significant change will occur in the situation of the Strait of Hormuz.”

Trump also suggested Sunday that talks would broach what he called the “de-nuclearization” of Iran. There has been no word from Tehran on that aspect of the negotiations.

World.title: Egypt, Kuwait FMs stress need to intensify efforts to de-escalate regional tensions
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty and his Kuwaiti counterpart Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah stressed, during a phone call on Sunday, Aug 2, 2026, the importance of intensifying regional and international efforts to de-escalate tensions, prevent the conflict from widening and support political and diplomatic tracks aimed at restoring regional security and stability.

The call came as part of ongoing consultations and coordination between the two brotherly countries on issues of mutual concern.

The two ministers exchanged views on the rapidly evolving regional developments and underscored the importance of maintaining close coordination and consultations in the coming period to support efforts aimed at containing tensions and preserving the region’s security and stability.

World.title: Finance Minister: Egypt to launch investment fund for expats next year
World.content:
Egypt plans to launch a dedicated investment fund for Egyptians living abroad next year, offering investment instruments with competitive returns and simplified subscription procedures, Minister of Finance Ahmed Kouchouk said on Saturday.

Speaking at the seventh annual Egyptians Abroad Conference, Kouchouk said the government is working with leading domestic and international investment banks to complete preparations for the fund.

He added that the government is also developing a digital platform with the Industry Ministry and the Investment and Foreign Trade Ministry to enable investors to establish companies more easily and encourage greater investment by Egyptian expatriates.

Kouchouk said Egypt is expanding digital government services and integrating artificial intelligence to simplify procedures and improve access for users in multiple languages.

He added that the government has launched a mobile application for real estate tax services and plans to roll out another app for real estate transactions later this month, both of which will be available to Egyptians abroad.

He also said Egypt aims to introduce virtual tax consultation services for Egyptians abroad through specialized tax service centers next year.

World.title: PM says President al-Sisi directs government to support Egyptians abroad
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said on Sunday, August 2, 2026, the government under the direct guidance of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi attaches great importance to supporting Egyptians living abroad, strengthening their ties with their homeland and expanding opportunities for them to contribute to the country’s development.

Speaking in a recorded address to the opening session of the seventh Egyptians Abroad Conference 2026, the Prime Minister said the government was committed to providing services and facilities for expatriates while protecting their rights, interests and dignity.

Madbouly conveyed President El-Sisi’s greetings to Egyptians overseas, describing them as “a cherished part of the Egyptian people” and praising their patriotism and enduring attachment to their homeland despite the distance.

He commended the Foreign Ministry’s efforts to provide services to Egyptians abroad and to strengthen communication with them in coordination with other state institutions.

The Prime Minister thanked Egyptians abroad for supporting the country through their remittances and investments, describing them as a key source of foreign currency that helped the economy withstand recent regional and global challenges.

Madbouly said recent events in the Middle East had created economic pressures, including disruptions to energy supplies, higher fuel prices, rising global inflation and increased tourism, transport, insurance and shipping costs, weighing on growth prospects worldwide, particularly in the Middle East.

He said Egypt had managed to weather those challenges with limited damage and expressed confidence that the economy would return to positive performance, citing expectations of stronger growth, higher employment, lower unemployment and fiscal deficits, and improved exports.

Madbouly added that Egypt continued to pursue comprehensive development across the country, prioritizing investment in education and healthcare, expanding industrial production, agricultural development and new urban communities to improve living standards, create jobs and attract investment.

He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to maintaining close ties with Egyptians abroad, expanding opportunities for them and responding to their needs, saying they remained partners in the country’s development and achievements.

World.title: FM, Gaza envoy discuss implementation of US-backed peace plan
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty discussed, during a phone call on Sunday, Aug 2, 2026, with High Representative for Gaza Nikolay Mladenov, the latest developments in negotiations to complete the implementation of the commitments under the US-backed Gaza peace plan.

The call came within the framework of ongoing consultations and coordination over the latest developments in the Gaza Strip.

Abdelatty stressed the importance of implementing all first-phase commitments, including ensuring the full, safe and sustained delivery of humanitarian aid, securing the Israeli withdrawal from the Strip, and advancing early recovery and reconstruction efforts.

The two sides also reviewed arrangements for the next phase, with Abdelatty underscoring the importance of the National Committee for Gaza Administration assuming its responsibilities from within the Gaza Strip to efficiently manage the transitional period and preserve the unity of the Palestinian territories.

Abdelatty further stressed the need for all parties to honor their commitments under the plan and refrain from taking any measures that could undermine its implementation, in a way that contributes to achieving security and stability and helps restore peace across the region.

World.title: 2026 Agriculture Show, exhibited innovation and technological products – Show goers
World.content:
Show goers and exhibitors at the just-ended 98th Zambia Agricultural and Commercial Show have commended this year’s event for showcasing innovative agricultural technologies, quality livestock and a wide range of local and international products.

Speaking in separate interviews with the media, attendees said the exhibition provided an opportunity for businesses to market their products while exposing members of the public to modern farming technologies, technology innovations as well as investment opportunities.

A trader in books, Jack Musa, said business started slowly during the first few days of the show but improved significantly towards the end.

Mr Musa noted that despite the slow start, the final two days recorded increased customer traffic, enabling exhibitors to recover some of their sales.

He, however, expressed concern over the declining reading culture in the country, attributing the trend to the growing influence of social media.

According to Mr Musa, he suggested that the government should consider establishing libraries in every school, both public and private, to encourage learners to develop a reading culture from an early age.

Other exhibitors interviewed by the media also expressed satisfaction with business performance, saying they realised significant profits during the exhibition.

Both Exhibitors, Show goers, traders as well as musicians and other artists spoken too by the media further praised the security arrangements during the event, noting that the presence of law enforcement officers before, during and after the show ensured a peaceful and safe environment for conducting business and enjoying the exhibition.

The 98th Zambia Agricultural and Commercial Show officially closed to the public today and will return next year.

The six-day exhibition, which ran from July 29 to August 3 at the Lusaka Showgrounds, attracted over 1,400 local and international exhibitors from over 20 countries, including China, Czech Republic, Germany and India was celebrated under the theme “Fostering Trade and Investment.”

World.title: Mbala Central and Saise Constituencies ballot papers arrives
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has delivered ballot papers for Mbala Central and Saise Constituencies in Mbala District ahead of the August 13 General Elections.

The verification exercise is underway in the presence of key stakeholders in the electoral process.

ECZ Personal Assistant, Wilfridah Banda, said the Commission is pleased with the strong stakeholder participation, noting that more than 10 representatives from political parties, civil society organisations and the media witnessed the arrival and physical verification of the ballot papers.

Ms Banda said the exercise demonstrates the Commission’s commitment to conducting a transparent and credible electoral process.

And Foundation for Democratic Process (FODEP) Mbala District Chairperson Bright Sikanyika. commended ECZ for the transparent verification exercise.

Mr Sikanyika added that the verification of ballot papers for the Saise Constituency had been completed successfully.

And National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) representative, James Mwambazi, also expressed satisfaction with the process, saying the transparency exhibited during the verification exercise had inspired confidence in the electoral process.

Verification of ballot papers is continuing under the supervision of Electoral Commission of Zambia officials in the presence of stakeholders.

World.title: Mukandila: “What Is It That They Are Scared Of” – ECZ Under Fire
World.content:
Zambia’s Electoral Commission is hiding the names of its own polling staff, the Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance claimed on Monday, opening a press briefing ten days before the country votes with a warning shot at the referee of the election itself.

Celestine Mukandila said district electoral officers had gone silent on when ballot papers would arrive in constituencies, breaching what he called an earlier agreement with the commission. “Speculation is ours to have,” he said, accusing the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) of leaving alliance agents blind days before polling.

He then escalated. Lists of newly recruited polling staff carried National Registration Card numbers but no names, Mukandila said, and lawyers for the alliance had already written demanding full disclosure. “What is it that they are scared of,” he asked, alleging the commission was shielding “political cadres” recruited to run the vote on behalf of the ruling UPND.

From there, the briefing turned toward the border. Mukandila issued what he called marching orders to party agents in the swamps of Chilubi Island, warning of unnamed foreign nationals allegedly brought in to vote. He named Isoka, where he claimed Tanzanians may hold Zambian voting documents, Vubwi and Malawians, Chavuma and Ikelenge and Congolese and Angolan nationals. No evidence was presented.

Mukandila closed his section with a direct threat to the head of state, declaring Zambians had already chosen Tonse-Pamodzi candidate Brian Mundubile as “the people’s president” and vowing to remove President Hakainde Hichilema “by the ballot” within ten days.

Binwell Mpundu, the alliance’s Presidential Affairs Chairperson, took the podium next with the briefing’s most explosive claim: three men sent abroad for VVIP protection training have disappeared since landing back in Zambia. He named them as Gideon Kalopa, Victor Muziamba and Dickson Tembo, saying they had travelled to Russia to train in physical protection for Mundubile and running mate Makebi Zulu, then vanished after clearing Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on their return.

Mpundu offered no evidence of who took them, but pointed at “the state” or “rogue elements” inside the UPND, and invoked the case of activist Black Apple in the same breath. He listed other alliance supporters he said were being held on what he called flimsy charges, including Kennedy Kamba and Simi Kalonga, and appealed directly to the international community to intervene.

Pressed for a hard number during the briefing’s question period, an NRPUP official confirmed three, said it could rise to four, but “not exceed five,” and conceded the missing men had left and re-entered Zambia lawfully through the airport with full documentation, a detail that sits awkwardly against the abduction claim.

Mpundu then pivoted to the campaign trail itself, alleging the convoy had been attacked repeatedly through the Copperbelt and Northwestern provinces, in places with police assistance, and referenced a personal clash with Yuyi Mwayi. He said the same violence would now be turned on the Western and Southern provinces, where the alliance campaigns next, and accused the UPND of trying to fracture the Tonse-Pamodzi arrangement by courting figures inside an allied party, ordering members to route all comment through party secretaries general only.

The tone shifted sharply for the briefing’s final act. Secretary General Zumani announced the alliance’s donation platform had raised close to K1 million in its first 24 hours, with a further K2.8 million pledged, before a payment aggregator abruptly cut the platform’s access. A new aggregator has since restored service, Zumani said, issuing a fresh mobile money code, 848704728#, working across MTN, Airtel and Zamtel, alongside Visa and a USDT (TRC20) cryptocurrency wallet aimed at diaspora donors who wish to remain anonymous.

Mukandila returned to defend the fundraising drive against UPND mockery, arguing every campaign runs on donor money and accusing the ruling party of hypocrisy, alleging its own war chest is linked to the ZNS “millimill” scandal and mining-sector patronage. “We don’t have any lives after this election if these people win,” he said, framing the donation drive as a way to keep Mundubile answerable to citizens rather than foreign backers.

World.title: Government to continue fostering development-President Hichilema
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has pledged that his administration will continue fostering development across the country.

President Hichilema explains that to attain this, his administration has come up with a number of interventions such as the Cash for Work programme and free education among other strategies.

The Head of State also cited the skills development component under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) stating that the move ensures young people are equipped with knowledge in lifelong skills in plumbing among other trades.

President Hichilema explained that his administration will work on constructing a skills training centre in Kasenengwa district, to ensure young people access the services locally.

The Head of State was speaking during a public gathering held at Kasenengwa Primary School Grounds in Kasenengwa District today.

“We will ensure that a skills training centre is constructed in the district so that people can train from here as opposed to going to other areas”, he said.

President Hichilema said the Chipata-Msoro road which has been problematic for some time will also be worked on in order to ease movements among residents.

“The Chipata-Msoro road has been on my mind therefore, don’t even doubt it because we will definitely work on it”, he said.

President Hichilema added that his administration is also working towards paying farmers that are supplying their maize to the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) in good time to enable them prepare for the next farming season adequately.

The Head of State has since called on electorates in the area to rally behind the United Party for National Development (UPND) in the forthcoming General Election to enable him deliver more development in the area.

World.title: Business community urged to tap into export opportunities- ZDA
World.content:
The Zambia Development Agency (ZDA) has urged the business community in the country to position themselves and take advantage of export financing opportunities in order to penetrate regional and international markets.

ZDA Director General, Albert Halwampa, notes that access to finance remains critical for businesses seeking to expand beyond the domestic market.

Mr Halwampa says businesses aspiring to access export markets must not only identify business opportunities but also demonstrate sound financial management, operational efficiency, adequate production capacity, credible markets and the ability to meet financing obligations.

The DG said this in a speech read on his behalf by ZDA Acting Director for Export Promotion, Ernest Chirwa, during a one-day workshop themed “Business Beyond Borders: From Local Enterprise to Regional and Global Opportunity.” In Lusaka today.

Mr Halwampa said the workshop seeks to help businesses understand the requirements for accessing export financing through the Zambia Export Development Fund (ZEDF).

He explained that ZEDF provides affordable financing to help businesses strengthen working capital, increase production, undertake value addition and fulfil export orders.

Mr Halwampa encouraged participants to actively engage during the workshop and take advantage of the opportunity to better understand the financing services available under ZEDF.

The ZDA Chief also commended the media for supporting efforts aimed at raising awareness of export financing opportunities available to Zambian businesses.

Meanwhile, Zambia Export Development Fund (ZEDF) Manager, David Chewe, said Zambian businesses have significant potential to grow beyond the domestic market and increase their participation in regional and international trade.

Dr Chewe said the workshop is intended to provide tailored information to businesses operating in Lusaka Province on how they can access export financing and exploit opportunities in export markets.

He described Lusaka as the country’s principal commercial and business hub, noting that its economy is driven by diverse sectors including manufacturing, agro-processing, trade, logistics, technology and professional services.

Dr Chewe observed that unlike other regions whose economies are largely dependent on mining or seasonal activities, Lusaka’s economy operates throughout the year, making it strategically positioned to drive Zambia’s export growth.

In his submission in a presentation entitled, unlocking export growth opportunities for Small and Medium Enterprises, manufacturers, traders, supplies and businesses in Lusaka Province, the ZEDF Manager, urged businesses in the province to take advantage of the financing facilities available through ZEDF to improve productivity.

Dr Chewe further noted with concern that most products produced lack value to their products hence the need to increase value addition to their competitiveness in an effort to penetrate regional and international markets.

World.title: UPND Former Vice President Dr Banda remembered as gallant leader
World.content:
The United Party for National Development (UPND) has remembered its late former Vice President, Canicius Banda, as a gallant leader who served the party well.

Dr Banda, who died on Thursday, July 30, 2026, has been described by the UPND Media Director, Mark Simuuwe, as a gallant political leader whose works left an indelible mark, having served as the party’s second-highest member.

Mr Simuuwe made these remarks shortly after signing in the book of condolence when he led a team to pay their respects to the late Dr Banda at the funeral house in Lusaka today.

He emphasised that Dr Banda’s unique way of explaining Zambia’s political landscape, particularly in the manner the government was running at the time the UPND was in opposition, was truly remarkable.

“Whoever has served in that capacity, the history of the party does not divorce from such a person. So we will remember him and his contribution,” Mr Simuuwe stated.

Mr Simuuwe noted that Dr Banda will go in the history books as one who explained Zambia’s political phenomenon under his name pilgrim.

“His works will remain active for as long as UPND remains active,” he noted.

He further highlighted that Dr Banda will be both missed in the context of politics as well as a former Vice President of the UPND.

Speaking shortly after the UPND Media team visited the funeral house in Meanwood Ibex in Lusaka today, Uncle to the late, Fidelis Sakala, highlighted that the family has lost a pillar of the family who will be greatly missed by all.

Mr Sakala also mentioned that further details concerning the burial programme will soon be announced by the family.

World.title: Lusangazi Central and Msanzala Ballot Papers arrive
World.content:
Ballot papers for the Lusangazi Central and Msanzala Constituencies have safely arrived in Lusangazi District under tight security ahead of the August 13, 2026 General Election, with the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) assuring stakeholders that all procedures were followed during the handover.

Lusangazi District Electoral Officer, Tembo Sekani, confirmed that the district had received all ballot paper boxes required for every polling station, covering the Presidential, Parliamentary, Council Chairperson and Ward Councilor elections.

Mr Sekani said the ballot papers were verified against the Material Issue Forms in the presence of political stakeholders to ensure the serial numbers corresponded with the official records.

He explained that the ballot papers are classified as sensitive election materials and have been placed under 24-hour security in a secure storage facility awaiting verification and subsequent distribution to polling stations.

Mr Sekani added that stakeholders would continue verifying the election materials before they are officially handed over to Presiding Officers for deployment to polling stations.

He assured voters that the ballot papers were secure and encouraged all eligible citizens to prepare to exercise their constitutional right to vote peacefully on polling day.

Meanwhile, Independent Parliamentary Candidate Election Agent, Mususa Mwambula, described the receipt of the ballot papers as transparent and satisfactory.

Mr Mwambulwa said political stakeholders were able to verify the number of ballot paper boxes received, thereby strengthening accountability and confidence in the electoral process.

He urged those responsible for safeguarding the ballot papers to maintain the same level of integrity until the materials are delivered to polling stations.

Mr Mwambulwa also appealed for equal treatment of all political contestants, regardless of party affiliation or independent status, and called on election officials to remain impartial throughout the electoral process.

And Aspiring Independent Candidate for Lusangazi Council Chairperson, Patrick Banda, commended the Electoral Commission of Zambia for conducting the exercise professionally and transparently.

Mr Banda who witnessed the arrival and handover of the ballot papers, said the process had inspired confidence among stakeholders.

He appealed to the Commission to continue providing round the clock security for the ballot papers until polling day and called on political players and members of the public to uphold peace before, during and after the elections.

The arrival of the ballot papers marks another key milestone in Lusangazi District’s preparations for the 2026 General Election, with verification of the materials expected to continue before their distribution to polling stations.

World.title: President Hichilema has effectively engaged communities-UPND
World.content:
United Party for National Development (UPND) Eastern Province Chairperson, Peter Phiri, says President Hakainde Hichilema’s ongoing public gatherings in Eastern Province has enabled the ruling party to engage communities and highlight government developmental projects.

Mr Phiri said the President’s second campaign visit to the province has provided an opportunity for people to interact directly with the Head of State and discuss issues affecting their communities.

He also commended the peaceful conduct of the 2026 General Election campaigns, saying political parties have largely campaigned without violence.

Mr Phiri attributed the calm atmosphere to what he described as the government’s commitment to peaceful campaigns and urged voters to maintain peace before, during and after polling day.

He said residents in the province have expressed appreciation for government programmes such as the Free Education, the School Feeding Programme and the enhanced Social Cash Transfer scheme.

Mr Phiri said the Government has also outlined a number of infrastructure projects for Eastern Province, including the planned upgrading of roads.

He said President Hichilema has indicated that the Chipata-Lundazi Road project has been awarded to a contractor who has already mobilized to site.

Mr Phiri further said the President has announced plans to upgrade sections of the road network in Chipata into a dual carriageway to help ease traffic congestion.

He added that the UPND intends to continue using the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) to finance community projects, improve feeder roads and expand development initiatives across the province.

Mr Phiri also cited the need to address human-wildlife conflict in areas bordering protected wildlife habitats, saying the government should strengthen measures to protect communities and support affected families.

Meanwhile, he urged voters in Eastern Province to support President Hichilema and UPND candidates in the August 13 General Election, arguing that the party has delivered on key development programmes during its time in office.

The President is expected to address campaign rallies in Kasenengwa, Chipangali and later Mfuwe as part of his campaign tour of Eastern Province.
